confirmed.title: An MT940 statement with no closing balance is silently dropped when another :20: follows
confirmed.description: case "20" replaces the current Statement without checking whether the previous one still has rows never closed by :62F:/:62M:. Only the last statement in the file gets the 'no closing balance' check, contradicting decision #13 and the class Javadoc, which say the whole file is rejected.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A file has message S1 (:60F:, :61: +100, no :62F:, e.g. cut during a concatenated download) followed by a complete message S2. parse() returns 1 row (S2) and no exception. S1's lines vanish, the import reports success, and cash figures are understated.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In case "20", throw Mt940FormatException if st != null && st.running != null && the statement was not closed.

verdicts.reasoning: I traced the path in Mt940Parser.java and the finding holds. Line 52, `case "20" -> st = new Statement(value.trim());`, replaces the current statement with no check on it. S1's rows sit only in `s.rows` (line 85) and are copied into the result only on :62F:/:62M: (line 103, `rows.addAll(s.rows); st = null;`). When S1 has :60F: and :61: but no :62F:, the next :20: drops S1 and its rows go with it. S2 then parses as normal: :60F: works because st is not null, and its :62F: check (line 97) compares only S2's own opening balance plus lines, so it passes. Only S2's rows are added. The truncation check after the loop (line 112, `if (st != null && !st.rows.isEmpty())`) only sees the last statement, which is now null, so it does not fire. `anyOpening` is true, so nothing is thrown. Result: parse() returns only S2's rows and S1's lines vanish without an error. This breaks accepted decision #13 in vault/00-Index/Решения.md ("по каждой выписке входящий остаток + операции = исходящему (:62F:). Иначе файл отклоняется целиком") and the class Javadoc (lines 21-22: "Each statement's lines must add up to its closing balance... otherwise the whole file is rejected"). The existing tests (Mt940ParserTest line 50, Mt940ImportIT line 52) only cover a mismatched :62F:, not a missing one in the middle of a file, so nothing catches this. Two minor points: S1's rows still use up row numbers, so S2's rows start at a higher number. And the file is rejected anyway if S1 sits between a valid statement and nothing else. But the stated scenario (S1 with no :62F:, then a complete S2) does silently lose data.

I confirmed this from the code. In Mt940Parser.parse, case "20" at line 52 runs `st = new Statement(...)` with no check on the statement it replaces. A statement's rows are only moved into the output list in the 62F/62M branch (line 103). The "no closing balance" check after the loop (line 112) only looks at the last `st`.

Walking through the scenario: S1 is :20:, :60F:, :61:, with no :62F:. S2 is a complete statement. When S1 reaches :60F:, anyOpening becomes true. When S2's :20: arrives, it throws S1 and its rows away. S2 balances and is added, and st becomes null. So the post-loop check passes and parse() returns only S2's rows, with no error.

The parser is really used: ImportService picks parsers through TabularParser.supports() for .sta/.mt940/.940 files, and PILOT_RUNBOOK runs the CLI on `ameria_2026-09.sta`. This is not a documented choice. Decision #13 ("rejected as a whole"), the README and the class Javadoc all say any statement that fails the opening+lines=closing rule must cause the whole file to be rejected. Line 113 shows the author meant to catch truncation, but only covers the end of the file. The existing tests (Mt940ParserTest) only check a wrong closing amount or a cut at the end, not a missing :62F: in the middle.

How often this happens: it needs a damaged multi-statement file, for example concatenated downloads, a hand-merged file, or a bank that writes a bare ":62:". That last case is a second path to the same bug: the FIELD regex `\d{2}[A-Z]?` parses ":62:" as tag "62", which falls into the ignored default branch, so every statement except the last is dropped without an error. Such input is unusual but realistic, and the result is lost money rows with an import that reports success. That breaks the explicit acceptance rule.

I am lowering severity to medium because it only happens with malformed or atypical input. It does not happen with normal, well-formed bank exports.

The finding holds. In Mt940Parser.java, line 52 (`case "20" -> st = new Statement(value.trim());`) replaces the current statement without checking it. A statement's rows only reach the result list in the :62F:/:62M: branch (line 103, `rows.addAll(s.rows)`). So if S1 has :60F: and :61: lines but no :62F: and is followed by :20: for S2, S1's rows stay in the dropped Statement object and never reach `rows`. The 'no closing balance' check after the loop (lines 112-113) only looks at whatever `st` is at end of file. When S2 closed correctly, `st` is null, so no exception is thrown. parse() returns only S2's rows and the import succeeds.

This is not intended behavior. Decision #13 in vault/00-Index/Решения.md (accepted) says MT940 is accepted only if, for every statement, opening balance + lines = closing (:62F:), and otherwise the whole file is rejected, because a missing line would silently distort the money figures. README.md lines 88-89 ("Each statement must satisfy opening + lines = closing, otherwise the whole file is rejected... nothing is written") and the class Javadoc say the same. The code breaks that invariant for any statement that is not the last one.

Mt940ParserTest only covers a wrong closing amount and complete multi-statement files. No test has an unclosed statement in the middle of a file.

Severity high is justified. The scenario is realistic (for example, a concatenated or partly cut download). The result is silent loss of bank-transaction data and understated cash figures, which is exactly what the founder's decision was meant to prevent.

confirmed.title: CSV is always decoded as UTF-8 with silent replacement; Windows-1251 values become U+FFFD and UTF-16 crashes in PostgreSQL
confirmed.description: InputStreamReader(UTF_8) replaces malformed bytes with U+FFFD and raises no error, and there is no BOM or charset sniffing beyond the UTF-8 BOM. Russian-locale Excel saves 'CSV (Comma delimited)' in cp1251.
confirmed.failure_scenario: cp1251 file 'Дата,Операция,Товар / 01.09.2026,Возврат,Хлеб' parses as {'����': ..., '��������': '�������'}. Cyrillic headers miss the mapping, so every row is rejected as 'Required field is empty'. With ASCII headers the values are silently garbled: returnMarkers ['Возврат'] no longer match so returns are booked as SALE, and 'ХЛ-001' and 'МК-001' both become '��-001', merging products and colliding ids. A UTF-16LE CSV yields headers with embedded NUL; Jackson writes \u0000 and PostgreSQL rejects the jsonb ('unsupported Unicode escape sequence', verified), crashing the import.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Detect UTF-16/UTF-8 BOMs. Decode with CodingErrorAction.REPORT and either fall back to a configured charset (e.g. windows-1251) or reject the file with a clear message.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. The code does what it describes.

CsvTabularParser.java:28 reads `var reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(in, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));`. An InputStreamReader built from a Charset uses the decoder's default REPLACE action, so bytes that are not valid UTF-8 turn into U+FFFD and no error is raised. Lines 29-32 only skip a UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF). Nothing in the parser detects the charset, handles a UTF-16 BOM, or lets the mapping set an encoding. A grep for charset, encoding and UTF finds only the hard-coded UTF_8 here and in Mt940Parser. The README, PILOT_RUNBOOK, decision log and architecture notes never say CSV must be UTF-8, so this is not documented, intended behavior.

Tracing the downstream effects:
- Values that come out garbled are used as-is. `CommitService.isReturn` (line 266ff) compares with `opRaw.trim().equalsIgnoreCase(m.trim())`, so 'Возврат' decoded as U+FFFD characters never matches a return marker and the row is booked as a sale.
- `productFor` looks up products by alias `(source, code)` and then `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, sku_code)`. In cp1251, 'ХЛ-001' is D5 CB 2D... and 'МК-001' is CC CA 2D.... Each lead byte is followed by a non-continuation byte, so each byte becomes one U+FFFD. Both codes become "��-001", so the two products merge into one SKU with no error.
- If the headers are Cyrillic, they no longer match the mapping's header names, so the mapped fields come back empty.

The UTF-16LE part also holds. The bytes FF FE become U+FFFD, and every ASCII character is followed by a NUL. The NULs end up in header and cell strings, `ImportService.jsonb(row)` passes them through `json.writeValueAsString(row.asMap())`, and Jackson writes them as \u0000. PostgreSQL jsonb rejects \u0000 ("unsupported Unicode escape sequence"), so the import crashes.

The cp1251 scenario is realistic in Armenia, where Russian-locale Excel and Cyrillic product names are common. The UTF-16 case is less likely, because Excel's "Unicode Text" export saves a .txt file that `supports()` rejects unless it is renamed to .csv. Even so, the core defect is real: the file is decoded wrongly without any error, which leads to returns booked as sales and merged SKUs.

I could not refute this finding; it is reachable in real use. On line 28, CsvTabularParser.parse wraps the input in new InputStreamReader(in, StandardCharsets.UTF_8). That decoder silently swaps malformed bytes for U+FFFD. The only charset handling is skipping a UTF-8 BOM (lines 29-32), and no charset setting appears anywhere in the code or the docs. The README, runbook and decision log say nothing about encoding, so this is not documented behavior. Reachability: ImportService.upload picks CsvTabularParser for any *.csv file name and passes it the raw uploaded bytes; the pilot CLI (PILOT_RUNBOOK lines 16-17) does exactly this. The founder doc (sections 37, 49-51, 57, 133) requires CSV import from HC/1C accounting exports and bank statements, and in an Armenian or Russian-locale Windows setup these are often cp1251. I checked the behavior with java: "ХЛ-001|МК-001|Возврат" encoded as windows-1251 and decoded this way gives "��-001|��-001|�..." and p[0].equals(p[1]) returns true. So two different product codes collapse into one value, and a 'Возврат' return marker no longer matches. All of this happens with no error. I also checked psql against retail_test: select '{"a\u0000":1}'::jsonb fails with "unsupported Unicode escape sequence". If the headers themselves are Cyrillic, every row is rejected, which is loud rather than silent. The UTF-16 case ends in an import crash, which is also loud. confirmed.title: decimal() applies the mapping's decimal separator blindly, so mismatched separators silently scale amounts by 10x-1000x
confirmed.description: With decimalSeparator '.', every ',' is deleted; with ',', every '.' is deleted. Grouping is never validated (e.g. a ',' followed by 1-2 digits cannot be a thousands group) and nothing is rejected as ambiguous. XlsxTabularParser renders numeric cells with DataFormatter(Locale.ROOT), always '.' decimal and ',' grouping ('1,234.50'), whatever the mapping says, while text-number cells from 1C/ArmSoft and Armenian-locale CSV exports use '12 500,00'. No single mapping setting is right for both, and the runbook says to copy the sample mappings (which use '.') and change only headers.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified with jshell against target/classes: with the default '.' mapping, '12 500,00' parses to 1,250,000, '12,50' to 1250, '1 234,56' to 123456 and '35000,5' to 350005. With ',' (what a hy-AM operator would pick, since Excel shows commas), XLSX cell 1234.5 formatted #,##0.00 renders '1,234.50' and parses to 1.2345, '12.5' to 125, and a General '0.5' kg to 5. No bad_number issue is raised; sales, COGS, ad spend or bank amounts enter the KPIs 10x-1000x off.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass XLSX numeric cells through unformatted (getNumericCellValue/BigDecimal) and apply the separator only to string cells. In decimal(), validate the grouping pattern against the declared separator and return empty (bad_number) for a value with the other separator in a decimal position (e.g. ',dd$' under '.') or both separators in the wrong order.

I traced the code and the finding holds. ValueConverters.decimal (lines 23-35) removes spaces and NBSPs. Then at line 27, if dec is ",", it runs `v = v.replace(".", "").replace(',', '.')`, and otherwise it runs `v = v.replace(",", "")` (line 30). Line 32 strips every remaining non-[0-9.-] character, and the result goes to new BigDecimal. Nothing checks how digits are grouped or flags a value as ambiguous, so the only way to get Optional.empty() (bad_number) is a value that fails to parse after stripping.

Hand trace with the '.' mapping, which all four samples in docs/samples/mappings/*.json use (`"decimalSeparator": "."`):
- "12 500,00" -> "12500,00" -> "1250000" = 1,250,000
- "12,50" -> 1250
- "35000,5" -> 350005

Hand trace with the ',' mapping: XlsxTabularParser line 22 uses `new DataFormatter(Locale.ROOT)` and line 48 passes `formatter.formatCellValue(cell)` text, never the raw numeric value. A #,##0.00 cell holding 1234.5 therefore arrives as "1,234.50", which becomes "1,23450" and then 1.2345. A General cell holding 0.5 becomes "05", which is 5.

All of these values pass as valid numbers and are committed with no issue raised. PILOT_RUNBOOK.md line 25 tells operators to copy a sample mapping and change only the headers, and line 30 says only unreadable numbers are rejected. Nothing in the README or the decision log documents this as intended. So a CSV exported with an Armenian or Russian locale under the default mapping inflates amounts 100x and more, and XLSX numeric cells under a ',' mapping are deflated or inflated, all without any error. Both cases feed wrong money values into the KPIs. The behavior is confirmed and high severity is justified.

With ',', it deletes every '.' and then turns ',' into '.'. It never checks the grouping pattern, so '12,50' under '.' becomes 1250 and '1,234.50' under ',' becomes 1.2345. Both come back as a valid Optional, so RowContext.decimal raises no bad_number and the row is committed.

2. XlsxTabularParser builds `new DataFormatter(Locale.ROOT)` and turns every cell into its formatted display text with formatCellValue. ROOT symbols always use '.' for decimals and ',' for grouping, whatever decimalSeparator the mapping says. Raw numeric values are never passed through. So on an XLSX import, ',' is wrong for every numeric cell with a fraction: '1,234.50' becomes 1.2345, '12.5' becomes 125, and a General-format 0.5 becomes 5. Text-formatted numbers in the same workbook (common in 1C/ArmSoft exports, e.g. '12 500,00') need ','. No single setting works for both kinds of cell.

3. Real use reaches it. The import CLI (PILOT_RUNBOOK step 2) feeds the parser output straight into CommitService. The runbook tells operators to copy a sample mapping, and all four samples use '.'. Its per-client steps only say to change headers, vatIncluded and accountRef, and never mention decimalSeparator. Under that default, an Armenian-locale CSV with values like '35000,5' or '12,50' is silently scaled up by 10x-100x.

Limits on impact: whole-number AMD amounts with no grouping parse correctly under either setting. The error needs fractional or grouped values, such as kg quantities, '.00' money formats, '#,##0.00' cells, or comma-decimal CSVs. These are common in Armenian accounting exports, so the scenario is realistic. The result is silent and corrupts money KPIs, so high severity stands.

All of these parse "successfully", so no bad_number/rejected issue is raised.

Nothing documents this as intended:
- README only mentions rounding.
- The decision log and architecture notes say nothing about separators.
- PILOT_RUNBOOK step 1 tells operators to copy the sample mappings (all of which use "decimalSeparator": ".") and change only the headers. That makes the mismatch likely for comma-decimal exports.
- The runbook also promises that an "unreadable number" makes the row rejected and keeps it out of the report. Silent 100x scaling breaks that promise.
- The founder doc (section 4 workflow, section 11) requires checking the import and showing an error list before KPIs are computed.

Coverage gap: ValueConvertersTest only tests inputs whose separator matches the mapping, so the mismatched case is never exercised.

Severity: high is justified. It needs a separator mismatch, but the runbook's own instructions lead there. When it happens, sales, COGS, ad spend and bank amounts silently enter the KPIs 100x-1000x off, with no warning.

confirmed.title: Bank credit/debit mapping flips the sign when the debit column holds negative numbers: an outflow is stored as an inflow
confirmed.description: In credit/debit mode (bank_statement_credit_debit_v1.json), amount = credit - debit, and the debit value is used exactly as it appears in the file. Many bank exports print the outgoing column as negative numbers ('-42 000,00') or in parentheses ('(42,000.00)'). decimal() keeps that sign, so subtracting the negative debit produces a positive amount. Nothing takes abs(), rejects negative debit/credit cells, or flags the row. The schema says debits are < 0. This is a separate field from the reported return-sign issue.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The 'Ելք' column holds -42000 for a rent payment, and the stored amount is 0 - (-42000) = +42000, so the expense is booked as income. A debit described 'POS acquiring commission' becomes a positive acquiring credit and is matched against sales. A -300,000 transfer to the client's own reserve account becomes positive, so ReconciliationService finds no mirrored pair (it needs a debit < 0). The incoming leg on the reserve account then stays counted as income, which is the double counting the founder criterion forbids. CashPositionService's balance chain also breaks (balance_after - amount no longer equals the previous balance), so the account shows 'ambiguous_order' and no balance.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use credit.abs() - debit.abs() and warn when a debit or credit cell is negative. Add an explicit mapping setting for the debit column's sign convention, and support a separate D/C indicator column.

**The subtraction.** `CommitService.bankTransaction` (around lines 210-215) uses the debit and credit values exactly as parsed:
```
BigDecimal credit = r.decimal("credit", false).orElse(BigDecimal.ZERO);
BigDecimal debit = r.decimal("debit", false).orElse(BigDecimal.ZERO);
amount = credit.subtract(debit);
```
There is no `abs()`, no `signum()` check and no `r.warn` on either value.

**The parser keeps the sign.** `ValueConverters.decimal` keeps a leading `-`, because its filter `replaceAll("[^0-9.\\-]", "")` leaves the minus in place. It also explicitly turns parentheses into a negative number:
```
boolean negative = v.startsWith("(") && v.endsWith(")"); ... return Optional.of(negative ? d.negate() : d);
```
So a debit cell of `-42000` or `(42,000.00)` becomes -42000, and the stored amount is 0 - (-42000) = +42000.

**Nothing else catches it.** Searching `src/main/java` for `signum` or `negative` turns up only the sales negative-quantity warning (`CommitService:116`), plus KPI and recon logic. No check exists on bank debit or credit cells. The mapping template `docs/samples/mappings/bank_statement_credit_debit_v1.json` maps `debit` to `Ելք` and has no setting for the sign convention.

**Downstream effects are real.**
- `ReconciliationService:57` skips any transaction with `debit.amount.signum() >= 0`. A flipped outgoing transfer therefore never becomes the debit side of a mirrored pair. The incoming leg on the other own account then stays external income, unless the own-account marker happens to catch it.
- `CashPositionService:80` computes `balanceAfter - amount`. A flipped sign breaks that chain and can lead to `ambiguous_order` with no balance shown.

**Why medium rather than high.** The failure depends on the bank format. It only happens with banks whose debit column holds signed (negative) or parenthesised numbers. The template's name already says "headers depend on the bank — confirm per client". The Ameriabank-style sample used in the tests (CommitServiceIT:140, ReconciliationServiceIT:144) appears to use positive debit values. The broken balance chain may also surface the problem indirectly as `ambiguous_order`. Still, when such a file is imported, outflows are silently booked as inflows, with no warning. That is a concrete, plausible defect.

confirmed.title: A corrected SKU or a voided document in a re-export leaves the old sale_line in place: the same sale is counted twice, or a phantom sale stays forever
confirmed.description: The line identity includes the SKU code, which can change on a document line. Nothing compares an overlapping re-export of a period with the rows already imported for that period. Changing a line's SKU in HC creates a new identity, a new source_record and a new sale_line, and the old sale_line under the old SKU stays. A document deleted or cancelled in HC is simply absent from later exports, and its sale_lines are never retired or flagged. ImportService only inserts or updates by identity (lines 70-89), and CommitService only inserts (lines 125-137). This breaks the founder criterion that re-importing the same document must not duplicate sales.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In week 1, document Հ-00042, line A-1046, qty 2, 84,000 is committed. The accountant then corrects the line to A-1047 in HC. Week 2's overlapping export contains Հ-00042 / A-1047, which is inserted as a new sale_line, and Հ-00042 / A-1046 remains. KPIs count 84,000 twice. A-1046 shows 2 phantom units sold, which inflates its velocity and can suppress SLOW_MOVER or trigger RESTOCK. A receipt voided in HC after week 1 stays in net sales permanently, with no warning.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Key lines on a stable line id (document plus line number, or document type, number and date) rather than on the SKU. When a file covers a date range or a set of documents, raise a 'missing_in_reexport' issue for previously committed rows in that range that are missing from the new export, or supersede them, instead of keeping them silently.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code path and it behaves as the finding says.

1. Identity includes the SKU. hc_sales_v1.json:23 sets `"idColumns": ["Փաստաթղթի համար", "Ապրանքի կոդ"]`. RecordIdentity.of joins those values with '/', so the week-1 row gets "Հ-00042/A-1046" and the corrected row gets "Հ-00042/A-1047". These are different identities.

2. ImportService.upload, lines 70-89: the corrected row has no conflict on (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id). It is inserted as a new source_record in the week-2 batch. The old "Հ-00042/A-1046" record is not touched, because the old SKU is not in the week-2 file. Nothing in the loop or after it compares this batch with records already imported for the same document or date range.

3. CommitService.commit, lines 42-45, reads only `source_records WHERE import_batch_id = :batch`. saleLine (lines 125-131) runs `INSERT INTO sale_lines ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id) DO NOTHING`. The new identity is inserted. The old sale_line under A-1046 has no UPDATE or DELETE path and is never retired.

4. Nothing excludes the stale row later. A grep for superseded, is_active, deleted_at and voided found nothing in the code or the migrations. KpiService (lines 49-51) sums every sale_line where `occurred_at >= :from AND occurred_at < :to`. So both lines are counted: 84,000 twice, and 2 phantom units on A-1046 that feed into velocity, days of stock and the SLOW_MOVER flag.

5. A receipt voided or deleted in HC is just missing from later exports. Nothing reacts to that absence, so its sale_line stays in net sales for good.

6. This is not documented as intended. The README and decisions #8 and #9 cover only an exact duplicate file, or the same identity arriving with different content. They say nothing about a changed identity or a deleted document. Founder criterion 11 requires that re-importing the same document must not duplicate sales, and that retroactive corrections (հետին թվով ճշգրտում) are tested. A document whose line SKU was corrected, then re-imported, produces duplicate sales, which breaks that criterion.

Why I lowered the severity to medium: the problem appears only when a line is corrected or a document is voided in HC after its first import. That is realistic but not every week. Also, the reconciliation against the accountant's closed-period report (criterion 4, ReconciliationService) would eventually show a numeric difference, so the double count is not completely invisible. The weekly KPIs and recommendations are still wrong until someone investigates.

Related problem, not part of this finding: even when the identity stays the same (for example, only the amount changes), saleLine's `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` means the new source_version never reaches sale_lines.

Real usage reaches this path. PilotCli.java:68 passes mapping.settings().idColumns() into ImportService.upload. The documented sample mapping hc_sales_v1.json, which PILOT_RUNBOOK step 2 tells you to copy for each client, sets idColumns = [document number, SKU code]. RecordIdentity.of joins these values as "doc/sku", so a line whose SKU changes gets a new source_record_id.

The runbook also shows period-range exports (HC_sales_2026-07-01_2026-09-30.xlsx) imported repeatedly, so overlapping re-exports are the normal workflow.

Nothing in main code removes or retires old rows:
- ImportService (lines 70-89) only upserts by identity.
- CommitService.saleLine inserts with ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id) DO NOTHING.
- A grep for DELETE FROM / UPDATE sale_lines finds only a reconciliation_matches delete.
- No missing-in-export detection exists anywhere.

KpiService (lines 40-55) sums every sale_line in the date range, grouped by sku_code. So after an SKU correction, the old line (doc/A-1046) and the new one (doc/A-1047) both count, and net sales are doubled for that line. A document voided in HC stays in sale_lines indefinitely, with no flag.

The docs don't present this as intended. The README idempotency section covers only identical files and identical rows. Re-importing the same corrected document then creates a duplicate sale, which contradicts the founder acceptance criterion in section 11 ("re-importing the same document does not create a duplicate sale"). The same section also lists backdated corrections ("հետին թվով ճշգրտում") as something that must be checked.

The trigger, an accountant changing an SKU or voiding a posted document in the accounting system, is ordinary behavior, not an impossible state.

1. **The line key includes the SKU.** In docs/samples/mappings/hc_sales_v1.json, idColumns is ["Փաստաթղթի համար", "Ապրանքի կոդ"]. RecordIdentity.of joins these into source_record_id. If an accountant changes the SKU on a line in HC, the line gets a new identity.

2. **Import only adds or updates.** ImportService (lines 70-89) inserts a source_record or updates it when the same identity arrives with different content. Nothing compares a re-export with what was already imported, so rows missing from a later export are never noticed.

3. **Commit only adds.** CommitService.saleLine inserts with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A new identity becomes a second sale_line. The sale_line under the old SKU is never retired, changed or flagged. Nothing in src/main/java checks for duplicate documents or tracks deletions.

**Failure scenario.** Document Հ-00042 is committed in week 1 with SKU A-1046. The SKU is later corrected to A-1047 in HC. Week 2's overlapping export creates a second sale_line, so KPIs and the weekly report count the 84,000 twice and show A-1046 with 2 sales that did not happen. A receipt voided after week 1 stays in net sales permanently.

- README says only that identical rows are not inserted twice and that the same identity with new content bumps the version of the stored source row (source_version).
- Decision #8 sets the key to the mapping's id column or a hash of the row. It says nothing about corrections or deletions.
- Decision #9 shows the team meant to handle restated sources: it versions source_records because Meta restates recent days. That handling never reaches sale_lines and does not cover deletions.

**Conflict with the founder doc.**
- Section 11 requires that re-importing the same document via CSV or API does not create a duplicate sale.
- Section 4 (line 39) says loading the same file twice must not double sales.
- Section 8 (line 90) lists a "duplicate document" data-quality check, and there is none.
- The re-export is the same document (Հ-00042), and its sale ends up counted twice.

**Severity.** High is defensible: revenue and SKU velocity are inflated silently in client reports, with no warning, and there is no way to fix it. The case where HC corrects or voids an earlier document is realistic in overlapping weekly exports. It does need an edit or void after the first import, so medium would also be arguable. confirmed.title: Unicode minus, en-dash and trailing/embedded parentheses are stripped silently, so negative amounts become positive
confirmed.description: replaceAll("[^0-9.\\-]", "") deletes U+2212 MINUS SIGN and U+2013 EN DASH instead of treating them as a sign, and no error is raised. A negative is otherwise detected only as a leading '-' or fully enclosing parentheses, so accounting-style negatives with a currency token ('(1 234,56) AMD', 'AMD (1234.56)') also lose their sign. Some formatted Excel or report exports use the typographic minus.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified in jshell: decimal("−5000") returns 5000, and '−1 234,56', '(1 234,56) AMD' and 'AMD (1234.56)' all come out positive. A bank debit '−42 000' is stored as a +42,000 credit, and a return or discount loses its sign.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Normalize U+2212/U+2013/U+2012 to '-' before stripping, and treat parentheses around the number (with surrounding currency or space tokens) as negative. Reject any value where non-numeric characters other than known currency or space tokens are removed.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code path and the finding holds. In ValueConverters.decimal (ValueConverters.java:21-39):
- L23 `v = raw.trim().replace(" ", "").replace(" ", "")` removes only ASCII spaces and NBSP.
- L24 `boolean negative = v.startsWith("(") && v.endsWith(")");` treats a value as negative only when parentheses wrap the whole string.
- L32 `v = v.replaceAll("[^0-9.\\-]", "");` silently deletes every other character, including U+2212 MINUS SIGN and U+2013 EN DASH.
- L35-36 `new BigDecimal(v)` succeeds, and a positive value comes back with no error.

Walking the inputs through it:
- "−5000" (U+2212): it does not start with '(', so `negative` is false. The dot setting removes no commas. L32 strips the minus, leaving "5000", and the result is +5000.
- "(1 234,56) AMD" with the comma setting: after L23 it is "(1234,56)AMD". It ends with 'D', so `negative` is false. L28 turns it into "(1234.56)AMD" and L32 into "1234.56", which is positive.
- "AMD (1234.56)": it starts with 'A', so `negative` is false, and it also comes out positive.

The empty-result check at L33 is never hit, so RowContext.decimal (RowContext.java:50-53) adds no "bad_number" issue. I found no upstream normalization of Unicode dashes anywhere in the code (searched for Normalizer, − and replace calls; only Mt940Parser has its own separate parsing). The value then feeds signed fields directly. In CommitService.bankTransaction (L210-211) `amount = r.decimal("amount", true)` takes a signed bank amount, so a "−42 000" debit is stored as a +42,000 credit. The discount and cogs fields at L102-104 are affected the same way. The existing ValueConvertersTest covers only an ASCII '-' and a fully wrapped "(12.5)", and no README or decision-log entry documents dropping the typographic minus as intended. How often this happens depends on exports writing amounts as text with U+2212, which is plausible for CSV and formatted report exports. When it does happen, the sign flips silently and goes into cash and KPI data with no warning. Medium severity is fair.

I could reach this through real usage, so the finding stands.

**Code path.** `RowContext.decimal()` calls `ValueConverters.decimal()` for every amount the import reads:
- sales: quantity, gross, discount, VAT and cogs
- bank: amount, credit/debit and balance
- ads: spend

Line 24 marks a value negative only when the whole string starts with '(' and ends with ')'. Line 32 then deletes every character except digits, '.' and '-'. That covers U+2212 MINUS SIGN, U+2013 EN DASH, unmatched parentheses and currency text. It raises no error, so `bad_number` is never reported.

**How real input reaches it.**
- `XlsxTabularParser` reads each cell with `DataFormatter(Locale.ROOT).formatCellValue()`, so a value arrives as the text Excel displays.
- The project expects currency tokens in values. `ValueConvertersTest` asserts that "35 000 ֏" parses as 35000.
- I ran Apache POI 5.5.1 (the version in `~/.m2`) on a cell holding -42000.5:
  - Format `#,##0 "AMD";(#,##0) "AMD"` displays as "(42,001) AMD".
  - Excel's built-in accounting currency format displays as "$   (42,000.50)".
- After spaces are removed these become "(42,001)AMD" and "$(42,000.50)". Neither both starts with '(' and ends with ')', so the parentheses are stripped and the parser returns +42001 and +42000.50.

**Effect on stored data.**
- **Bank import with an `amount` column:** a debit is stored as a positive credit. This is the inflow-for-outflow error the finding describes, and it carries into cash position and reconciliation.
- **Sales import:** a negative quantity loses its sign, so the "negative quantity → RETURN" rule in `CommitService.saleLine` never fires. Gross and discount amounts also lose their sign.

**What is less certain.** The typographic minus (U+2212) would most likely come in through CSV text. I did not prove that a specific Armenian bank export uses it, but nothing in the code guards against it. The parentheses-plus-currency case alone is confirmed reachable through the XLSX parser.

**Docs.** Nothing in the README, runbook or decision log documents this as intended behaviour.

I confirmed this from the code. In ValueConverters.decimal (lines 21-40), line 23 strips only NBSP and ASCII space. Line 24 treats a value as negative only when the whole trimmed string starts with '(' and ends with ')'. Line 32, replaceAll("[^0-9.\\-]", ""), then deletes every other character, including U+2212 MINUS SIGN and U+2013 EN DASH.

- "−5000" (U+2212) becomes "5000" and parses as +5000.
- "(1 234,56) AMD" becomes "(1234,56)AMD". It does not end with ')', so negative=false. The parens and "AMD" are then stripped, giving +1234.56.
- "AMD (1234.56)" goes the same way.

No error is raised. The method's own Javadoc says Optional.empty() means "could not convert", and RowContext.decimal only raises bad_number when the result is empty. So the sign flip is silent: no validation issue and no warning.

Where it does harm:
- **Bank import, single 'amount' column** (CommitService.bankTransaction lines 209-211). A typographic-minus debit is stored as a positive credit. ReconciliationService uses amount.signum() to classify debits and credits (internal-transfer pairing at lines 57-61, acquiring credits at line 95). The debit side of an own-account transfer then never pairs, and the row can be counted as an acquiring credit or as income. That breaks the founder acceptance criterion (section 11) that a transfer between a client's own two accounts must not become double income or expense.
- **Sales.** A negative quantity is the only signal that turns a sale row into a RETURN (lines 116-121), so a quantity written with U+2212 stays a SALE. That breaks the section 11 criterion that returns and discounts are handled correctly.

Nothing in the documentation makes this intended. README, the decision log and the architecture notes never describe how the sign is parsed. ValueConvertersTest covers only "(12.5)", "35 000 ֏" and similar cases. It has no test for a Unicode minus or for parentheses next to a currency token.

The severity of medium fits. The default and most common exports use the ASCII hyphen-minus, which works. The typographic minus and accounting-style parentheses next to a currency token come from formatted Excel or report exports, so the trigger is realistic but not universal. When it fires, a debit is silently stored as a credit with no error raised, and both the reports and the reconciliation are wrong.

confirmed.title: Days of stock uses the latest snapshot per (sku, warehouse) ever, so sold-out or stale stock is reported as current
confirmed.description: onHand takes DISTINCT ON (sku_code, warehouse) the newest row with as_of_date <= to, independently for each pair, with no lower bound and no age flag. Inventory exports usually list only non-zero balances, so when a SKU sells out and is missing from the newest snapshot, its quantity from an older snapshot is used. The same happens for a warehouse that stopped reporting.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Snapshot 2026-09-01: X/Main = 40. Snapshot 2026-09-30 lists other SKUs but not X, because it sold out. X sold 40 units in September (velocity 1.333/day). KPI: onHand = 40 and daysOfStock = 30.0, so no RESTOCK (threshold 14). Real stock is 0, and RESTOCK priority 1 is suppressed exactly for the SKU that ran out.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use the latest snapshot date per warehouse (or per source batch) and treat SKUs absent from it as 0. Flag snapshots older than N days before `to`, and downgrade RESTOCK/SLOW_MOVER when that happens.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. The code path does what the finding describes.

**The on-hand query** (KpiService.java:66-72):
`SELECT DISTINCT ON (sku_code, warehouse) sku_code, warehouse, quantity FROM inventory_snapshots WHERE as_of_date <= :to ORDER BY sku_code, warehouse, as_of_date DESC`
- Each (sku, warehouse) pair gets its own newest row.
- There is no lower bound on the date and no check against the tenant's latest snapshot date. The per-SKU snapshot date is never returned or flagged.
- The results are then summed per SKU with `onHand.merge(...)`.

**The import does not zero out missing SKUs.** CommitService.inventory (lines 140-165) inserts one row per file row with `ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING`. A SKU that is absent from a newer snapshot file keeps no zero row, so the older row stays the newest one for that pair.

**Tracing the stated scenario** (to = 2026-09-30):
- The query returns X/Main = 40 from the 2026-09-01 snapshot, so `stock = 40` (line 147).
- Net units are 40 over 30 period days (lines 134, 146), so velocity = 1.3333333333.
- `daysOfStock = stock.divide(velocity, 1, HALF_UP)` = 30.0 (line 153).
- `slow` is false, because 30 is not greater than 90.
- RESTOCK in RecommendationEngine.java:37-38 needs `daysOfStock < restockBelowDays` (14), and 30.0 is not below 14. RESTOCK is therefore suppressed for a SKU whose real stock is 0.

**The staleness guard does not catch it.** The engine's `stale` check is `ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(dataAsOf, today) > staleAfterDays`, and `dataAsOf` is a tenant-level date (the README calls it "days since last import"). The fresh 09-30 import makes the report look current while X's figure is 29 days old.

**Documented behavior vs. acceptance criteria.** The README says "Days of stock = latest snapshot per (sku, warehouse)", so the formula itself is documented. It does not cover SKUs missing from a newer snapshot. That gap conflicts with founder acceptance criterion §11: a recommendation must not be presented as reliable when its source is old. Section 3 also requires showing data freshness for every recommendation. Here, a 29-day-old per-SKU figure is presented as current stock and drives or suppresses RESTOCK and SLOW_MOVER.

**Precondition and severity.** The scenario assumes inventory exports leave out zero balances. That assumption is realistic: typical 1C balance reports drop zero rows, and a warehouse can also stop reporting. Medium severity fits, since this is a misleading stock figure and a missed restock signal, not data loss.

Real usage can reach this. Nothing in the code or schema blocks it.

1) KpiService.java:66-72 runs `SELECT DISTINCT ON (sku_code, warehouse) ... WHERE as_of_date <= :to ORDER BY sku_code, warehouse, as_of_date DESC`. It has no lower bound and never compares a pair's date with the newest snapshot date for that warehouse or batch. A pair that is missing from a newer snapshot therefore keeps its old quantity.

2) The import path inserts these rows as described. CommitService.inventory (lines ~139-166) writes one row per file row with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A new snapshot never zeroes or supersedes SKUs it leaves out. There is no "absent from latest batch = 0" logic anywhere. The schema (V2 inventory_snapshots) has no such constraint either, only uq(tenant, source_system, source_record_id).

3) The pilot scenario in the founder doc (90 days of data, stock balances imported repeatedly) produces several snapshots. Stock-balance exports that leave out zero-balance items are common, for example HDM-Trade balance reports. A warehouse that stops reporting gives the same result. No data-quality check compares the SKU set of a new snapshot with the previous one.

4) Downstream, nothing catches it. RecommendationEngine (lines 37-45) gives RESTOCK only when daysOfStock < restockBelowDays (14). With stale onHand = 40 and velocity 1.333, daysOfStock is 30, so RESTOCK is suppressed. The stale check uses dataAsOf, which RecommendationService.java:46-48 takes from max(import_batches.ingested_at), not from the snapshot's as_of_date. A recent import of any file type marks the data fresh, so an old per-pair snapshot is never downgraded. The same old quantity can also raise a false SLOW_MOVER, because `slow = stock > 0` when velocity is 0.

5) The README (line 54) documents the formula as "latest snapshot per (sku, warehouse) summed". That describes the aggregation, not a decision to carry sold-out balances forward. The decision log has no entry accepting this. It conflicts with the founder's definition, "Days of stock = available stock ÷ velocity". It also conflicts with the AI rule that old data must be presented as last-known. The existing test (KpiServiceIT:108-125) only covers a SKU that appears in both snapshots, so it says nothing about this case.

The finding's scenario follows directly from the code. Medium severity is fair: it hides a priority-1 RESTOCK for exactly the SKU that is out of stock. Its only premise is that exports omit zero rows or that a warehouse stops reporting, which is realistic, not impossible state.

I confirmed the code does what the finding says. In KpiService.java (lines 66-72), each (sku_code, warehouse) pair gets its newest row with `as_of_date <= :to`. There is no lower bound on the date and no check that the row comes from the newest snapshot, so a pair missing from the latest file keeps its quantity from any older file. Nothing records how old that snapshot is. No KPI flag marks an old snapshot (KpiFlags has only NO_INVENTORY_SNAPSHOT). RecommendationEngine's `stale` comes from RecommendationService.dataAsOf = max(ingested_at) over all import_batches, so a fresh sales or ads import makes a months-old inventory figure count as current. In the finding's scenario, KPI gives onHand=40 and daysOfStock=30.0. That is not below restockBelowDays (14), so RESTOCK is suppressed and the recommendation is not marked stale.

Is this intended? README line 54 does document the formula as "latest snapshot per (sku, warehouse) summed". The KpiServiceIT test daysOfStock_fromLatestSnapshotAndNetVelocity only checks that an older row is replaced when the same pair appears again; it does not cover a pair that drops out of the newest file. The decision log (Решения.md) has no entry on snapshot completeness or inventory freshness. The vault KPI note records only one deliberate omission: excluding stockout days from velocity.

The documented formula still conflicts with the founder's requirements:
- Section 11: a recommendation must not be published as reliable when the source is stale.
- Section 8 / the vault KPI note: days of stock = *available* stock, and figures must not be published as reliable when the source is older than the freshness threshold.

The code has a freshness check for bank balances (CashPositionService.STALE_AFTER_DAYS), but there is no equivalent for inventory. So documenting the formula does not excuse the missing freshness handling.

Caveat: the sold-out-SKU-missing-from-export variant assumes the export leaves out zero balances. I did not verify that for the HS-Trade or CSV formats. The stale per-pair carry-forward with no flag (a warehouse that stopped reporting, or any SKU absent from later files) is unconditional and enough to confirm the defect. Medium severity fits: no data is lost, but it gives a misleading operational signal that suppresses the highest-priority (priority 1) recommendation, RESTOCK.

confirmed.title: KPIs add sales and ad spend across currencies and label the total with an arbitrary group's currency
confirmed.description: Spend is coalesce(sum(spend),0) over campaign_daily with no filter on its currency column. Sale-line groups are summed regardless of max(sl.currency), and KpiReport.currency is overwritten by whichever group comes last in a result with no ORDER BY (line 104). No flag is raised, and CommitService stores the per-row currency from the file, so a USD export goes in without complaint. Multi-currency being deferred to a later phase means the code should reject or flag mixed currencies, not add them; criterion 2 requires currency to be handled correctly.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The Meta ad account bills in USD (header 'Amount spent (USD)', Currency=USD): 500.00 USD is summed into an AMD report as 500 AMD, so contribution is overstated by about 194,500 AMD under a header 'currency AMD'. Separately, an online channel exports 3 lines of 100 USD next to 2,000,000 AMD of shop sales: net sales are reported as 2,000,300 and the summary may read 'արժույթ՝ USD' if a USD group comes last; unit prices and AD_TEST figures for that SKU mix USD and AMD.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add currency to the GROUP BY / filter sums by currency. If any row's currency differs from the tenant base_currency, exclude it and add a CURRENCY_MIXED flag, or compute per currency, or refuse to compute contribution.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The code does what the finding says.

KpiService.java:
- Lines 40-51: sale_lines are grouped by `sl.sku_code, sl.operation_type, sl.vat_included, (sl.cogs_amount IS NOT NULL)`. Currency is not in the GROUP BY. It is only selected as `max(sl.currency) AS currency`, so one group can hold USD and AMD rows together.
- Line 75: `SELECT coalesce(sum(spend), 0) FROM campaign_daily WHERE date BETWEEN :from AND :to` has no currency filter, although campaign_daily has a NOT NULL currency column (V2 migration).
- Lines 90 and 104: `String currency = "AMD";` is then overwritten inside the loop by `currency = (String) g.get("currency");`. The value comes from whichever group is last, and the query has no ORDER BY. That value goes into KpiReport.currency (line 171). WeeklyReportService.java:115 prints it as `արժույթ՝ " + k.currency()`.
- Lines 106-131: amounts from every group are added into grossSales, discounts, netSales and per-SKU totals without checking currency. No currency flag exists or is set. The KPI flags used are FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED, NO_INVENTORY_SNAPSHOT, NO_MARKETING_DATA, ADS_NOT_FINAL, VAT_UNKNOWN, COGS_MISSING, LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE and VARIABLE_COSTS_ASSUMED.
- Line 169: `contribution = grossProfit.subtract(variableCosts).subtract(spend)` subtracts the mixed-currency spend.

Nothing upstream stops mixed currencies. CommitService.java:105 takes the currency from the file (`r.text("currency") != null ? r.text("currency") : s.currencyOr("AMD")`) and stores it with no warning. Lines 203 and 251 do the same for campaign_daily and bank rows. No validator looks at currency.

So a Meta export in USD with spend 500.00 is stored as campaign_daily.currency='USD' and subtracted as 500 from an AMD contribution. USD sale lines are likewise added to AMD net sales, and the report's currency label can come out as USD.

The README, PILOT_RUNBOOK and decision log say nothing about assuming a single currency or rejecting other currencies. The founder doc treats multi-currency as phase 4 (line 139). But line 39 asks the validation step to catch wrong currency, and acceptance criterion line 146 requires currency to be handled correctly. Deferring multi-currency does not cover silently adding different currencies together.

Medium severity is right. It needs a non-AMD export, which is realistic for Meta ad accounts billed in USD. When it happens, contribution margin and net sales are silently wrong and shown under a misleading currency label.

I could not refute this finding: real usage reaches it and nothing guards against it.

1. Non-AMD values get into the database. CommitService.campaignDaily (around line 203) and saleLine (line 105) store `r.text("currency")` straight from the mapped file column, falling back to settings.currencyOr("AMD"). The sample Meta mapping (docs/samples/mappings/meta_campaign_daily_v1.json) maps `currency` to the "Currency" column. Step 1 of PILOT_RUNBOOK tells the operator to replace every header with the client's exact header. So for a USD ad account the operator maps "Amount spent (USD)", and every row is stored with currency='USD'. No validation code checks currency against tenants.base_currency (grep finds no other currency handling in commit/validation). In the DB, currency is just char(3) NOT NULL with no CHECK constraint. Meta ad accounts billed in USD are common for Armenian advertisers, so this is a normal input, not an edge case.

2. The KPI query mixes them. KpiService line 75 is `SELECT coalesce(sum(spend),0) FROM campaign_daily WHERE date BETWEEN ...`, with no currency filter. The sale_lines query (lines 40-52) does not group by currency and only takes max(sl.currency). Line 104 overwrites `currency` on every loop pass, so the report gets the label of whichever group comes last, and the query has no ORDER BY. Line 169 subtracts spend from gross profit with no conversion.

3. Nothing flags it. KpiFlags has no currency or mixed-currency flag. WeeklyReportService line 115 prints "արժույթ՝ " + k.currency() as the report's currency.

4. It is not documented as intended. The vault notes only defer multi-currency to phase 4. Neither they nor the decision log say mixed currencies should be added together silently. Founder doc section 4 (line 39) requires imports to be checked for wrong currency, and acceptance criterion line 146 requires currency to be handled correctly. Here a 500 USD spend is subtracted as 500 AMD in an AMD-labelled contribution with no warning, which is a misleading report. The scenario is reachable through the documented CLI flow.

I confirmed this from the code. It is not intended behavior.

1. KpiService.java:75 sums campaign_daily.spend with no filter on currency.
2. The sale_lines group query takes max(sl.currency) for each group but does not group by currency.
3. The loop then adds every group into the same totals. At line 104 it sets `currency` to whatever the last group returns, and the query at line 40 has no ORDER BY, so that is an arbitrary group.
4. KpiReport passes that currency on, and WeeklyReportService.java:115 prints it as "արժույթ՝ X".
5. KpiFlags has no currency flag.
6. CommitService (lines 105, 203, 251) stores whatever currency each row in the file carries. A grep of mapping, parse and commit found no check that compares it to a base currency.

The docs do not describe this as intended. The README only covers per-currency totals for cash (line 109). The decision log (Решения.md) never mentions currency. The vault says multi-currency is phase 4, but deferring it does not allow silently adding different currencies together.

It also contradicts the founder doc. Item 4 at line 39 says imports must be checked for a wrong currency ("սխալ արժույթը"). The acceptance criterion at line 146 says currency must be handled correctly ("արժույթը ... ճիշտ են մշակվում").

The scenario is realistic. Meta ad accounts often bill in USD, and the CAMPAIGN_DAILY mapping accepts a currency column. If that happens, contribution is wrong by about 389x the USD spend (roughly 389 AMD per USD), and the report is still labeled AMD. Medium severity is right: an all-AMD pilot gives correct numbers, but a USD ad export or a USD channel gives a misleading report with no warning.

confirmed.title: Negative stock gives a HIGH/PUBLISHABLE RESTOCK with negative days of stock, and negative warehouses net against positive ones
confirmed.description: CommitService.inventory() accepts negative quantities with no warning; KpiService sums them across warehouses and divides by velocity. RecommendationEngine (line 37) fires RESTOCK whenever daysOfStock < 14, so a negative value always qualifies, with no data-quality flag. Negative stock in HC/ArmSoft is a posting error (sales booked before receipts), and the founder's criterion 2 requires negative balances to be handled correctly.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The snapshot has SKU A/Main = -3 and A sells 1/day: onHand = -3, daysOfStock = -3.0, and the engine builds RESTOCK priority 1, HIGH and PUBLISHABLE; the template says 'stock is -3 units, will last about -3 days' (confirmed in a scratch copy with -5 / -2.5). Separately, Main = +10 and Second = -10 sum to onHand 0, so a RESTOCK goes out while 10 units sit in Main and the posting error is hidden.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Warn 'negative_stock' at commit. In KPI, flag NEGATIVE_STOCK per SKU and do not net warehouses below zero. Turn such SKUs into NEEDS_DATA (a question to the warehouse) instead of RESTOCK.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the full path and the finding holds. I could not refute it.

1. **Commit accepts negative stock silently.** `CommitService.inventory()` (lines 140-166) reads quantity with `r.decimal("quantity", true)`. The only warnings it adds are for missing cost or missing as_of_date. Nothing checks the sign, so a negative value is inserted unchanged. `ValueConverters.decimal` even turns "(3)" into -3. The schema has no check either: V2 declares `quantity numeric(18,3) NOT NULL` with no CHECK constraint. Contrast the sales path, where CommitService line 116-119 does warn `negative_quantity`; there is no equivalent for inventory.

2. **KPI sums negative stock across warehouses.** In `KpiService`, the onHand query uses `DISTINCT ON (sku_code, warehouse)`. It then calls `onHand.merge(sku, ..., (a, b) -> a[0].add(b[0]))`, a plain sum. So Main=+10 and Second=-10 give 0, and Main=-3 alone gives -3.

3. **Negative stock becomes negative days of stock.** KpiService lines 150-154: `stock` is not null and `velocity.signum() > 0`, so `daysOfStock = stock.divide(velocity, 1, HALF_UP)` gives -3.0. No flag is added; `KpiFlags` has nothing for negative stock.

4. **The engine fires RESTOCK.** `RecommendationEngine` line 37: `x.onHand() != null && x.daysOfStock() != null && x.dailyVelocity().signum() > 0 && x.daysOfStock().compareTo(restockBelowDays) < 0`. Both -3.0 and 0.0 pass, so it builds RESTOCK with priority 1. In `build()`, confidence starts at HIGH and status at PUBLISHABLE. They drop only on LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE (to MEDIUM) or stale data. So with at least 14 days of sales and fresh data, the result is HIGH and PUBLISHABLE. Even with fewer days it is still PUBLISHABLE, only MEDIUM.

5. **The template prints the negative numbers.** `TemplateExplanationProvider` line 40-42 writes on_hand and days_of_stock straight into the text ("մնացորդը -3 հատ է … կբավարարի մոտ -3 օր").

**Why this counts as a defect.** The founder's acceptance criteria (CLAUDE_RETAIL_AI_PLATFORM_CONTEXT_HY.md line 146) require that "բացասական մնացորդը ճիշտ են մշակվում" (negative balance is handled correctly). README, the runbook and the decision log say nothing about negative stock, so this is not documented intended behavior. One small caveat: HIGH confidence needs at least 14 days with sales. Otherwise the recommendation is MEDIUM but still publishable. That does not change the conclusion.

I could not refute this. Real imports reach it, and nothing in the code path stops it.
1. Input: CommitService.inventory() (lines 140-165) reads quantity with r.decimal("quantity", true). It never checks the sign and raises no warning. Only sale rows have a negative_quantity check (lines 116-119). The DB column inventory_snapshots.quantity is numeric(18,3) NOT NULL with no CHECK constraint (V2 line 69). ValueConverters even parses accounting-style "(3)" as a negative number. So a negative balance from an HC/ArmSoft export is stored as is.
2. KPI: KpiService lines 65-72 take the latest snapshot per (sku, warehouse) and merge them by plain addition. Main = +10 and Second = -10 therefore net to 0. At line 153, daysOfStock = stock / velocity whenever velocity > 0, so stock -3 at 1/day gives -3.0. No flag is added for negative stock; KpiFlags are only set for missing snapshot and low sample.
3. Recommendation: RecommendationEngine line 37 fires RESTOCK when onHand != null, daysOfStock != null, velocity > 0 and daysOfStock < restockBelowDays. Any negative value passes. build() starts at HIGH / PUBLISHABLE. It drops to MEDIUM only on LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE and to NEEDS_DATA only on stale data. Nothing looks at the sign of the stock. The sort also puts the most negative days_of_stock first, so these crowd out other recommendations. TemplateExplanationProvider line 40 turns on_hand into the "մնացորդը X հատ է" text, so the negative number goes out to the user.
4. Not documented as intended: README, the decision log and the architecture notes say nothing about negative stock, and no test covers it. Founder acceptance criterion 2 (CLAUDE_RETAIL_AI_PLATFORM_CONTEXT_HY.md line 146) explicitly requires negative balances ("բացասական մնացորդը") to be handled correctly.
The scenario is realistic: negative balances from sales posted before receipts are common in Armenian accounting exports. Severity medium fits: the result is a misleading recommendation and a hidden data-quality problem, not data loss.

I confirmed this from the code, and nothing in the project documents says it is intended.

1. **Negative stock is accepted silently.** `CommitService.inventory()` (CommitService.java:140-166) reads `quantity` and checks only that `as_of_date` and `cost` are present. It never checks the sign, so it raises no warning or error for a negative value. In V2 the `inventory_snapshots.quantity` column is `numeric(18,3) NOT NULL` with no CHECK constraint.

2. **Warehouses are netted together.** `KpiService` (lines 66-72) takes the latest snapshot for each SKU and warehouse, then merges them with `a[0].add(b[0])`. A warehouse with +10 and another with -10 add up to 0.

3. **Negative days of stock are passed through without a flag.** `KpiService` (lines 150-153) computes `daysOfStock = stock / velocity` whenever velocity is above zero, so -3 stock at 1 unit/day gives -3.0. It adds no flag; the only inventory flag in KpiFlags is `NO_INVENTORY_SNAPSHOT`.

4. **The engine publishes a confident restock.** `RecommendationEngine` (line 37) fires RESTOCK whenever `daysOfStock < restockBelowDays`, so any negative value qualifies. `build()` only lowers confidence for `LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE`, stale data, and VAT on AD_TEST. With enough sales history and fresh data, the result is priority 1, HIGH and PUBLISHABLE. The sort on `days_of_stock` also puts negative-stock SKUs at the top of the list.

**Is it intended?** README line 54 describes the formula as "summed ÷ net units per day" but says nothing about negative balances. The decision log (Решения.md) covers negative and positive only for MT940 bank reversals. Nothing documents what should happen when a snapshot is negative.

**Founder criteria.** Section 11, criterion 2 of the founder doc says, in Armenian: "returns, discounts, VAT, currency, rounding and **negative balance** are handled correctly". The code has nothing that handles a negative balance, so this goes against an explicit acceptance criterion.

**Severity.** Medium is right. The output is a misleading high-confidence, publishable recommendation that says "will last about -3 days". It also hides a posting error and can trigger a restock while stock is actually sitting in another warehouse. This does not lose data or breach tenant isolation, so it is not high or critical.

confirmed.title: Inventory snapshot identity ignores as_of_date, so a quantity returning to an earlier value is never snapshotted
confirmed.description: When the stock file has no date column, as_of_date comes from mapping settings and is not part of the raw payload or of the content-hash identity. A row identical to any earlier week's row is a no-op in source_records: it stays on the old batch and is not read by the new batch's commit, so no snapshot is written for the new date. KpiService then takes DISTINCT ON (sku, warehouse) with the latest as_of_date.
confirmed.failure_scenario: 01.09: SKU A / Main qty 10. 08.09: qty 5, a new hash, snapshot of 5 for 08.09. 15.09: qty 10 again, the same hash as 01.09, so no 15.09 snapshot is written. The KPI uses 5 instead of 10: days of stock are halved and a false RESTOCK is issued.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Include the effective as_of_date (from settings) and target entity in the payload or identity, and treat a snapshot file as a complete state for its date.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. I traced it end to end and it holds.

1. **Row identity leaves out the snapshot date.** In ImportService.upload, the record id comes from `RecordIdentity.of(row, idColumns)`. With no idColumns set, that is `contentHash(cells)` over the file's cells only. The payload is `row.asMap()`. The settings date (`s.asOfDate()`) is applied later, in CommitService.inventory, and is never added to the payload or the hash.

2. **A repeated row stays on its old batch.** The upsert is `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id) DO UPDATE ... WHERE source_records.raw_payload IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.raw_payload`. On 15.09 the row `A, Main, 10` has the same id and the same payload as on 01.09, so no update happens. `import_batch_id` stays on the 01.09 batch.

3. **The new commit never reads it.** CommitService.commit reads only `WHERE import_batch_id = :batch AND status <> 'rejected'`, so the 15.09 commit skips that row.

4. **The snapshot table blocks it too.** Even if the row were read, inventory() inserts with `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id) DO NOTHING`. Per V2, `uq_inventory_source` is UNIQUE on (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id), and as_of_date is not part of it. The 01.09 snapshot already has that id, so no 15.09 row could be written.

5. **The KPI picks up the wrong quantity.** KpiService uses `SELECT DISTINCT ON (sku_code, warehouse) ... WHERE as_of_date <= :to ORDER BY sku_code, warehouse, as_of_date DESC`. That returns the 08.09 row with qty 5, not the actual 10. RecommendationEngine issues RESTOCK when `daysOfStock < restockBelowDays`, so a halved stock count can trigger a false restock recommendation.

Two refinements:
- **With a single SKU, the file-level check fires first.** The 15.09 file is byte-identical to 01.09, so the `file_sha256` duplicate check returns early and PilotCli prints "Duplicate file ... Nothing changed." The outcome is the same: there is still no 15.09 snapshot. With more SKUs the file differs and the row-level path above applies.
- **Setting idColumns makes it worse.** For example, with sku and warehouse as idColumns the id becomes "A/Main". The source record is updated, but the inventory insert hits DO NOTHING on that id, so no snapshot is written after the first one.

None of the docs I checked describes this as intended: the README, the decision log and the architecture notes. The README calls the writers idempotent and computes days of stock from the "latest snapshot per (sku, warehouse)". That presumes each upload produces a snapshot dated by its file, so this is a real defect. I found no test covering repeated snapshot quantities across dates.

I traced the path end to end and the bug is reachable through normal use.

1. Entry point. `PilotCli.importFile` calls `ImportService.upload(..., mapping.settings().idColumns())` and then `CommitService.commit`. The `MappingSettings.asOfDate` field exists precisely for an INVENTORY_SNAPSHOT file that has no date column. Nothing in the README, the runbook or the decision log says a stock file must carry a date column.

2. Record identity. With no idColumns, `RecordIdentity.of` returns `contentHash(cells)`, built only from the parsed cells. The date from settings is not included. On 15.09 the stock file differs from the 01.09 file elsewhere, so the file-level sha check does not catch it. The SKU A / Main / 10 row, however, hashes exactly as it did on 01.09.

3. Source records. The upsert is `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE raw_payload IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.raw_payload`. The payload is identical, so nothing is updated and the row keeps its 01.09 `import_batch_id`.

4. Commit. `CommitService.commit` reads only `source_records WHERE import_batch_id = :batch`, so the row is never seen and no 15.09 snapshot is written. Even if it were read, `inventory()` inserts with `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id) DO NOTHING` against `uq_inventory_source` (V2 line 73). The 01.09 snapshot already holds that `source_record_id`, so the insert would still do nothing.

5. KPI. `KpiService` selects `DISTINCT ON (sku_code, warehouse) ... WHERE as_of_date <= :to ORDER BY as_of_date DESC`, so it picks the 08.09 snapshot with qty 5 instead of the real 10. That understates days of stock and can fire a false RESTOCK.

A variant with idColumns (for example sku/warehouse) fails the same way, or worse. The record id stays fixed, so after the first week the inventory insert always hits ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and no newer snapshot is ever written.

The finding's step-by-step scenario matches the code exactly. It needs no impossible state, only weekly stock exports without a date column and the mapping's `asOfDate` changed for each import, which is how the setting is meant to be used.

I confirmed this from the code and found nothing in the docs that makes it intended behaviour.

How the row identity is built:
- `ImportService.upload` calls `RecordIdentity.of(row, idColumns)`. With no id columns, the id is a sha256 of the row's cells only.
- The mapping-settings `asOfDate` is not part of that hash and not part of `raw_payload`.

What happens when the same row comes back:
- The `source_records` upsert has `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE raw_payload IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.raw_payload`. A row with identical content is a full no-op, so it keeps its old `import_batch_id`.
- `CommitService.commit` only reads rows `WHERE import_batch_id = :batch`, so that row is never passed to `inventory()` for the new batch.
- It would be blocked a second time anyway: `inventory_snapshots` has `UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id)` (V2 `uq_inventory_source`), and the insert uses `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
- `inventory()` (lines ~141-160) does read `as_of_date` from the file or from `s.asOfDate()`, but the date is never used to tell snapshots apart.
- If the whole file is byte-identical to an earlier upload, the `file_sha256` check returns the old batch before anything else runs.

Effect on the KPI:
- `KpiService` (lines 66-72) takes `DISTINCT ON (sku_code, warehouse) ... ORDER BY as_of_date DESC`.
- The scenario holds: 01.09 qty 10 (H1) → 08.09 qty 5 (H2, new snapshot) → 15.09 qty 10 (H1 again, nothing written). The latest snapshot stays at 08.09 = 5, so on-hand is understated by half and the days-of-stock / restock signal is wrong.

Docs checked:
- README line 54 says "latest snapshot per (sku, warehouse)", which assumes every upload records a snapshot for its date.
- The decision log has no entry on inventory snapshot identity. The architecture notes only say that a re-upload of an identical file is a no-op. There is no samples or runbook entry accepting that a row whose quantity returns to an earlier value silently drops the new date's snapshot.
- Founder doc line 100 defines days of stock as the *available* (current) balance divided by velocity. Using a stale quantity contradicts that.

Severity: medium is right. It is silent and gives a misleading stock KPI and recommendation. It needs a specific but realistic pattern (no date column, date set in settings, a quantity returning to an earlier value), and it does not lose data or cross tenants.

confirmed.title: Out-of-order imports overwrite newer or final data with older values and bump source_version
confirmed.description: Both the source_records upsert and the campaign_daily upsert (CommitService 190-198) apply any differing content unconditionally. Nothing records or compares export time, and is_final is recomputed from the date rather than used to protect the row. Whichever file is imported last wins, even when it is older.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The export taken 08.10 (final Meta numbers for 01-09.09) is imported, then the operator backfills a missed weekly export taken 10.09 with preliminary numbers for the same days. Every row differs, so source_records and campaign_daily are overwritten with preliminary spend, source_version goes to 2 as if it were the newer restatement, and is_final stays true. The report shows outdated spend as final, breaking the 'late ads reports' acceptance item.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the export or ingest timestamp per version and only apply a newer version. Never overwrite is_final rows from an older file; report the conflict instead.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the path and the failure occurs as described.

1. ImportService.upload, lines ~76-83: the source_records upsert is `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, source_system, source_record_id) DO UPDATE SET raw_payload = EXCLUDED.raw_payload, import_batch_id = EXCLUDED.import_batch_id, ... source_version = source_records.source_version + 1 ... WHERE source_records.raw_payload IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.raw_payload`. The only guard is that the content differs. Nothing stores or compares the export date or the file's period. The older backfill file has a different SHA, so it gets past the import_batches duplicate check. Its rows then overwrite the payload and move import_batch_id to the new batch. If idColumns are not set, RecordIdentity falls back to contentHash, so the rows go in as new records under the new batch instead. Either way they are committed.

2. CommitService line 44 commits `FROM source_records WHERE import_batch_id = :batch`, so the older rows reach campaignDaily().

3. CommitService lines 184-198: `boolean isFinal = date.isBefore(LocalDate.now(...).minusDays(28));` is computed from the calendar date only. The upsert `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, platform, campaign_id, date) DO UPDATE SET spend = EXCLUDED.spend, ... source_version = campaign_daily.source_version + 1, is_final = EXCLUDED.is_final ... WHERE campaign_daily.spend IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.spend OR ...` applies any differing values unconditionally. An existing is_final=true row has no protection.

Scenario check, with today = 2026-10-09: days 01-09.09 are older than 28 days, so isFinal=true. First the 08.10 export with final values is imported. Then the 10.09 export with preliminary values is backfilled. Spend differs, so the row is overwritten with the preliminary spend and source_version goes to 2. KpiService line 75 sums that spend. The ADS_NOT_FINAL check on line 82 (`date >= :fb`) only looks at the last 28 days, so these days are not flagged. The report shows the outdated spend as final, with no warning.

This is not covered by documented intent. README line 43 and decision #9 say only that a *restated* day bumps source_version, because Meta recalculates recent days. They assume the last import is the newest, and nothing documents or accepts an older file winning. Founder section 8, line 88, says to show differences and not silently overwrite data, and section 11, line 152, requires that late ads reports be handled. Both conflict with this behavior.

It does need an operator to import files out of order, but backfilling a missed weekly export is realistic. Medium severity is appropriate.

I could not refute this. Normal use reaches it, and nothing in the code, the schema or the docs prevents it.

1. A batch is skipped as a duplicate only when its file_sha256 matches an earlier batch (ImportService 44-51). An older export with different numbers has a different hash, so it is parsed and committed like any new file.

2. CommitService.campaignDaily (around lines 190-206) upserts ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, platform, campaign_id, date). The only guard is that spend, impressions, clicks or results differ. It never looks at an export timestamp or ingest order, and no such timestamp exists: the migrations only have an ingested_at that defaults to now(). So the older preliminary numbers replace the newer final ones, and source_version goes up by one.

3. is_final is set from EXCLUDED.is_final, which is computed only as "date is more than 28 days before today". Today is 2026-10-09, so the days 01-09.09 count as final. The overwritten preliminary values are therefore stored as final. KPI only raises ADS_NOT_FINAL for the last 28 days, so the report shows the stale spend with no warning.

4. In source_records (ImportService 72-87), what happens depends on the id columns. If the mapping names id columns such as campaign_id/date, the same identity matches and the row is overwritten the same way: raw_payload and import_batch_id are replaced and source_version is bumped. If it names none, the default content-hash identity creates new rows instead. Either way, campaign_daily is corrupted, so the core defect does not depend on the mapping.

5. The design notes do not cover this. README line 43 and decision #9 describe restatement as "same identity, different content means UPDATE with source_version+1". Both assume the newer file is imported last. Neither the README nor the runbook requires files to be imported in chronological order or mentions backfill. Founder acceptance criterion §11 requires late-arriving ads reports and backdated corrections to be handled. Under the code as written, whichever file is imported last wins, even an older export, which goes against that criterion.

Uploading a missed older weekly export after a newer one is a realistic mistake in a manual pilot. I agree with severity medium.

The defect is confirmed in the code. The source_records upsert in ImportService.java (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE raw_payload IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.raw_payload, around lines 72-85) and the campaign_daily upsert in CommitService.java (am/retailai/commit/CommitService.java lines 186-199; the finding names the wrong package) both overwrite whenever content differs. Neither looks at when the export was taken or at the existing is_final value. is_final is just recomputed from the date (line 184: date older than now minus 28 days). That means an older export uploaded later replaces the newer final numbers, bumps source_version as if it were a restatement, and keeps is_final=true. The previous payload is gone because there is only one row per identity and no history.

Documented intent does not cover this case. README lines 43-44 and decision #9 in Решения.md say a restatement (same identity, different content) updates with source_version+1, because Meta restates the last 28 days. That design quietly assumes files arrive in time order. Nothing in README, PILOT_RUNBOOK, the decision log or the tests (only KpiServiceIT.adSpendFromTheLast28Days_* checks the flag) addresses an older file arriving after a newer one. The founder doc goes against the current behavior. Line 88 says that when data differs, show the difference and queue it for explanation, and never delete or silently overwrite. Acceptance item line 152 says retroactive corrections and late ads reports must be checked.

The scenario is realistic. At onboarding, an operator uploading a backlog of overlapping weekly Meta exports in any order produces final-flagged spend that depends on upload order, with no warning. The 'updated' count is normal for ad files, so it does not alert anyone. Medium severity is fair: the KPIs and ad spend are misleading but plausible-looking. There is no crash or isolation breach, and the trigger depends on the order files are uploaded.

confirmed.title: account_ref is not a real account identity: one account splits into two refs (label vs masked number), and two accounts with the same last 4 digits merge
confirmed.description: account_ref is either the free-text label from the mapping or maskAccount(raw) = 'acct ***' plus the last 4 digits (lines 258-261), or just 'acct ***' when there are fewer than 4 digits. The bank_transactions unique key (tenant_id, account_ref, txn_id), CashPositionService (groups by account_ref) and ReconciliationService mirrored-pair detection (skips credit.accountRef.equals(debit.accountRef)) all treat this string as the account id. No canonical account entity links a label to a number, and the masked form is not unique.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Following the runbook, the operator imports BANK_statement.csv (accountRef 'Main AMD account') and ameria_2026-09.sta (stored as 'acct ***0000') for the same Ameria account with overlapping dates: TRX-88213 is stored twice and CashPositionService sums two accounts, reporting 2 x 2,148,000 AMD. Conversely, two accounts at different banks ending in the same 4 digits imported with bank_mt940_v1.json both become 'acct ***0000': a transfer between them is never paired as internal (counted as income and expense, breaking the own-account criterion), cash position mixes their lines, and a matching customer reference on the other account is dropped by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Introduce a bank_accounts table keyed by an HMAC/sha256 of the full account number, resolve both labels and file numbers to it, key bank_transactions and grouping by account id, and keep 'acct ***1234' for display only.

verdicts.reasoning:
The code path behaves as the finding says. CommitService.java:223 is `String accountRef = s.accountRef() != null ? s.accountRef() : maskAccount(r.text("account_ref"));`, and maskAccount (lines 258-261) returns `"acct ***" + last 4 digits`, or just `"acct ***"` when there are fewer than 4 digits. That string is the only account identity anywhere downstream:
- The unique key is `UNIQUE (tenant_id, account_ref, txn_id)` (V2 migration line 109), used with `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, account_ref, txn_id) DO NOTHING`.
- CashPositionService groups by `account_ref`, builds one balance per ref, and sums the refs into currency totals when their dates match.
- ReconciliationService line 60 skips a pair when `credit.accountRef.equals(debit.accountRef)`.
- No BankAccount table exists, although the data-model note lists one.

**Split case (confirmed).** The repo's own sample mappings produce it:
