The only AI criterion is about causal attribution of marked orders ("not because of the ad"), and the CAUSAL list covers that. The ban comes from the project's own design (README, decision #15, the Javadoc), not from an acceptance criterion.

It is still worth fixing before llm.enabled=true goes to pilot clients, because the guard is the stated safeguard and the eval plan in "Eval 20 кейсов" relies on it.

confirmed.title: Guard checks numbers as a loose set, not tied to their meaning, so a fact can be relabelled
confirmed.description: Every number in the text only has to equal some fact; which fact it stands for is never checked, so the LLM can attach a real number to the wrong meaning and still pass.
confirmed.failure_scenario: AD_TEST facts are net_price 35,000, cogs 22,000 and max_acquisition_cost 11,000. The LLM writes 'մեկ վաճառքի ձեռքբերման արժեքը չգերազանցի 35 000 դրամը' ('acquisition cost per sale must not exceed 35,000'). It passes because 35,000 is a fact, and the marketer gets a cap three times the real margin.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For key facts (max_acquisition_cost, days_of_stock), require the exact number next to its label phrase, or have the LLM output structured slots filled from the facts deterministically.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code and the described pass does happen. ExplanationGuard.check (lines 41-49) removes the SKU code, SKU name and dates, then runs NUMBER (line 24) over what is left. A token only fails if `interpretations(token).stream().noneMatch(v -> matchesAny(v, allowed))`. `allowed` (allowedNumbers, lines 65-74) is a flat Set<BigDecimal> built from `r.facts().values()` (exact value, plus rounded to 0 and 1 decimals) plus the integers 0..10. Fact keys are thrown away, so no number is ever tied to its label.

For AD_TEST, RecommendationEngine lines 65-70 put net_price_per_unit, cogs_per_unit, variable_cost_per_order, max_acquisition_cost and on_hand into facts. With the founder's example (35,000 / 22,000 / 2,000 / 11,000 / 126), the text 'մեկ վաճառքի ձեռքբերման արժեքը չգերազանցի 35 000 դրամը' goes like this:
- '35 000' matches the grouped branch of NUMBER.
- interpretations() gives 35000.
- norm(35000.00) is in `allowed`.
- None of the CAUSAL or GUARANTEE phrases appear.
So GuardResult passes. GuardedExplainer.explain (lines 32-37) then returns the LLM text as-is (guard-passed, no fallback reason), and the marketer sees an acquisition-cost cap of 35,000 instead of 11,000. ClaudeExplanationProvider only asks the model in its system prompt to 'Use only numbers that appear in facts'. Nothing in code checks which fact a number stands for.

Why not 'medium': (1) The guard's Javadoc (line 17) and README line 98 describe exactly this set-membership rule, so it is a known limit of the design, not a coding slip. (2) It needs the LLM to attach a number to the wrong meaning, which the prompt tells it not to do. (3) No acceptance criterion in section 11 of the founder doc requires checking which fact a number belongs to. Still, the guard says it exists to stop false acceptances ('a false acceptance costs the client's trust', line 20), decision #15 makes it the only output check, and the miss lands on a spending cap the marketer acts on. So I keep it as a real but low-severity hole in a defence-in-depth check, not a refuted finding.

I'm refuting this as a defect, with medium confidence. The finding describes the code correctly, but that behavior is the documented contract, and the founder's acceptance criteria don't require more.

What the code does: ExplanationGuard.check (lines 41-49) puts every fact value, plus its rounding to 0 and 1 decimals, into one set. A number in the text passes if it equals anything in that set. The guard never looks at which fact a number is attached to.

Can real usage reach it? Yes, but only when the LLM is switched on:
- LlmConfig builds GuardedExplainer(null) by default (llm.enabled=false). In that mode only TemplateExplanationProvider runs, and it puts each number next to the right label (TemplateExplanationProvider lines 43-47).
- With llm.enabled=true, ClaudeExplanationProvider's text goes through this guard. AD_TEST facts are net_price_per_unit, cogs_per_unit, variable_cost_per_order, max_acquisition_cost and on_hand (RecommendationEngine lines 66-70). So in principle a sentence that gives net_price as the acquisition-cost cap would pass.

Why that is intended, documented behavior rather than a defect:
- The class Javadoc spells out the rule as "every number in the text must equal a fact (exactly, or rounded to 0/1 decimals), a period date, or a small count 0..10".
- README line 97-98 describes the guard as "numbers only from facts, no causal claims without an experiment, no guarantees".
- Decision log #15 says the LLM only rephrases engine facts and the guard checks every answer. It never promises that a number is tied to its meaning.
- The guard does exactly what is documented.
- None of the section 11 acceptance criteria require numbers to be bound to their labels. The only AI-specific criteria are no "thanks to the ads" claims without an experiment, and tenant isolation. Both are enforced (the CAUSAL list and the experimentCompleted check).

The failure scenario is also hypothetical. It needs the opt-in LLM to go against its system prompt and mislabel a number. It doesn't come from any input, state or parser output the code produces. At most this is a known limit of a membership-only guard, a design improvement worth noting at low severity rather than a reachable bug that contradicts the spec.

This is a real gap, and nothing in the docs says it was meant to work this way.

Code: ExplanationGuard.check (lines 41-49) builds one flat Set<BigDecimal> from all fact values (allowedNumbers, lines 65-74). That set holds each value, its 0- and 1-decimal roundings, and the numbers 0..10. Each number token in the text only has to match some entry in the set. Nothing links a number to the fact key it stands for. So for an AD_TEST with net_price 35000, cogs 22000 and max_acquisition_cost 11000, the sentence "acquisition cost must not exceed 35 000" passes all three checks: it has no causal wording, no guarantee wording, and 35000 is in the set. GuardedExplainer (lines 32-37) then returns the Claude text as the accepted explanation, which is stored and shown to the owner.

Is it intended or documented? No.
- The README describes the guard as "numbers only from facts". The decision log (#15) says the LLM "only rephrases facts" and every answer is checked by the guard. The guard's own Javadoc says "a false acceptance costs the client's trust".
- No document admits that the guard cannot catch a number placed against the wrong label. The eval coverage doc does not list it as a known gap either.
- The design's purpose is that numbers come only from the deterministic engine. Text that pins the price to the "max acquisition cost" label quietly defeats that purpose while still passing.
- The founder doc (section 8) limits AI to explaining deterministic results. Section 11 has no criterion that excuses misleading AI text.
So the gap is not covered by any documented intent.

Severity: I would lower it to low.
- The LLM is off by default (README; decision #16 is only "proposed" and waits on backlog item G, the Anthropic key plus legal sign-off).
- The scenario needs the model to break an explicit prompt rule. The prompt sends named fact keys and says to use only the numbers that appear in facts.
- No action is automatic. Recommendations only record a human decision (Decision; eval case 11), so a wrong cap reaches ad spend only if a person acts on the text by hand.
- Still, if the LLM is turned on, the result would be a misleading report that the guard is supposed to prevent. So it is a real defect, but low impact today.

confirmed.title: Per-SKU 'low velocity sample' uses the shop-wide count of sales days
confirmed.description: LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE is added to each SKU when the tenant-wide daysWithSales < 14. A SKU's own number of selling days is never considered, so a velocity based on one sale day gets no flag as long as the shop sells something most days. This is the only flag the engine uses to lower RESTOCK/SLOW_MOVER confidence.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The shop sells daily. SKU X had one bulk sale of 30 units on 2026-09-12 and nothing else in September, with 10 on hand. Velocity is 1.0/day and days_of_stock 10, so RESTOCK is issued at HIGH confidence on a single sale event, with no warning on the SKU sheet.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Count distinct sale days per SKU in the SQL and set the SKU's LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE from that count.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code and the finding holds.

1. KpiService.java lines 57-63 compute `daysWithSales` once for the whole tenant: `SELECT count(DISTINCT (occurred_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Yerevan')::date) FROM sale_lines WHERE occurred_at >= :from AND occurred_at < :to`. The query has no sku_code filter or grouping, and the per-SKU aggregation SQL (lines 41-52) never counts distinct sale days per SKU.

2. Line 158, inside the per-SKU loop, is `if (daysWithSales < 14) a.flags.add(KpiFlags.LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE);`. It reads the shop-wide count, so every SKU gets the same answer whatever its own sales history is.

3. Velocity (line 143) is `netUnits / periodDays`, where periodDays is the calendar length of the period. In the scenario, 30 units sold in one bulk sale over a 30-day September window gives velocity 1.0. With stock 10, `daysOfStock = 10.0` (line 149).

4. RecommendationEngine.java lines 37-44 issue RESTOCK when `daysOfStock < s.restockBelowDays()`. The default in RecommendationSettings.java:6 is `new RecommendationSettings(14, 14, 3)`, and 10 < 14, so RESTOCK fires.

5. `build()` (lines 98-101) starts with `Confidence c = Confidence.HIGH;` and lowers it only via `if (flags.contains(KpiFlags.LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE)) c = Confidence.MEDIUM;`. For RESTOCK and SLOW_MOVER, the only other thing that lowers confidence is staleness. The shop sells on at least 14 days, so the SKU carries no LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE flag, and RESTOCK comes out as HIGH / PUBLISHABLE even though the SKU sold on a single day.

Nothing in the documentation makes this intended. README:96 and the vault only describe the 14-day staleness rule. KpiFlags.java:9 ("fewer than 14 days of sales history in the period") and the Armenian label ("sales days are fewer than 14, the velocity estimate is weak") describe the reliability of the velocity estimate, and the code attaches that flag to each SKU's sheet. The founder's KPI rule (section 7, days of stock must account for zero-demand and stockout days) also suggests per-SKU sales history matters. A per-SKU flag computed from a shop-wide count therefore overstates confidence on the SKU sheet and in RESTOCK/SLOW_MOVER recommendations.

Medium severity is fair. It produces a misleading HIGH-confidence recommendation, not data loss, and a human still approves every recommendation.

I could not refute this finding: ordinary imported sales data reaches it, and the code works as described.

**What the code does**
- In `KpiService.compute`, `daysWithSales` is one tenant-wide number: `count(DISTINCT occurred_at::date) FROM sale_lines` with no `sku_code` filter (lines 57-63).
- Line 158 then adds `LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE` to every SKU when that tenant-wide number is below 14. Nothing in the method counts how many days a single SKU actually sold.
- Velocity is net units divided by the number of calendar days in the period (`periodDays`).
- `RecommendationEngine.build` (line 101) lowers confidence for RESTOCK and SLOW_MOVER only when `LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE` is set. Otherwise only stale data lowers it. The VAT and formula-confirmation checks apply to AD_TEST only.

**The finding's scenario holds with the defaults**
- Defaults are `restockBelowDays` = 14 and `staleAfterDays` = 14.
- Period 2026-09-01..30, so `periodDays` = 30. The shop sells on 30 days, so `daysWithSales` = 30 and the flag is never set.
- SKU X has one line of 30 units and an inventory snapshot of 10. Velocity = 30/30 = 1.0, so `daysOfStock` = 10.0, which is below 14.
- Result: RESTOCK with confidence HIGH and status PUBLISHABLE, built from a single sale event, and the SKU carries no velocity warning.

**Reachability**
- Nothing upstream prevents this. The data is plain `sale_lines` rows from a normal import, plus an inventory snapshot.
- An existing test (`RecommendationEngineTest` around lines 102-104) confirms that `LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE` is the switch that drops RESTOCK to MEDIUM.

**Not documented as intended**
- Neither the README nor the decision log (`Решения.md`) says the per-SKU flag is deliberately tenant-wide.
- The flag's comment ("fewer than 14 days of sales history in the period") and its report label ("sales days are fewer than 14, the velocity estimate is weak") present it as a statement about how reliable the velocity is.
- The founder's spec (section 7, days-of-stock formula) says days of stock must account for zero-demand days and stockout days. A SKU that sold on one day out of 30 has 29 zero-demand days, and the confidence rule ignores them.

**Severity**
Medium is reasonable: a high-confidence restock recommendation is published on overstated grounds. The figures themselves are not wrong, and 30 units in a month is real demand.

The code does what the finding says. In KpiService.java, `daysWithSales` comes from one shop-wide query, `count(DISTINCT occurred_at::date) FROM sale_lines` over the period, with no per-SKU grouping. Line 158 then copies that one value onto every SKU: `if (daysWithSales < 14) a.flags.add(LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE)`. Nothing in the code counts how many days a single SKU sold on.

RecommendationEngine.build() starts every recommendation at HIGH confidence. For RESTOCK and SLOW_MOVER, the only thing that can lower it is this SKU flag (moving it to MEDIUM) or stale data (moving it to LOW). The other downgrades, for formulas not confirmed and unknown VAT, apply to AD_TEST only.

The failure scenario checks out with the default settings:
- RecommendationSettings.defaults() sets restockBelowDays to 14.
- For September (30 days), one sale of 30 units gives velocity 30/30 = 1.0 per day.
- With 10 on hand, days of stock is 10, which is under 14.
- The shop sells on 14 or more days, so the flag is never added and RESTOCK goes out at HIGH confidence and PUBLISHABLE.

I could not find any document that makes this intended:
- README's formula_v0 section says nothing about this flag.
- The decision log (Решения.md) has no entry about it.
- 'KPI и формулы.md' lists only stockout-day exclusion and ad allocation as deliberately not implemented. It does not mention sample size per SKU.
- The KpiFlags comment ("fewer than 14 days of sales history in the period") and the report label ("sales days are fewer than 14, so the velocity estimate is weak") describe sample quality. Copying a shop-wide count onto each SKU does not support that per-SKU reading.

The founder doc goes against this behaviour:
- §2 says every recommendation must show its degree of confidence.
- §7 says days of stock must take zero demand into account.
- §11 says recommendations must not be published as reliable on weak inputs.

None of the existing tests (KpiServiceIT, RecommendationEngineTest) cover a SKU with few sale days in a shop that sells every day.

Medium severity is right. The result is a misleading HIGH-confidence restock advice, not data loss or a breach. It is limited because a human must approve every recommendation, nothing runs automatically, and supplier_lead_time is always reported as missing.

confirmed.title: Velocity divides by the full calendar period even when it extends past today or past the last imported sale
confirmed.description: periodDays is from..to inclusive with no clamp to today or to the last sales date. Days after the last imported sale (a source gap, or a period ending in the future) count as zero-sales days, and nothing compares data coverage with the period, though 'source gap' is a required data-quality check (founder section 6). Velocity is understated and days of stock inflated, which suppresses RESTOCK and creates false slow movers; LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE only lowers confidence and does not restore a suppressed recommendation.
confirmed.failure_scenario: --from=2026-10-01 --to=2026-10-31 run on 2026-10-09 with sales through 10-08: the SKU sold 16 units in 8 days (2/day) and has 20 on hand. Computed velocity = 0.516 and daysOfStock = 38.7, so no RESTOCK; the true figure is 10 days. Similarly, sales exported only through 2026-09-19 give a September velocity 37% too low, and SLOW_MOVER may be issued at HIGH.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use min(to, today, last sale/import coverage date) - from + 1 as the denominator, or flag and downgrade when coverage ends before the period end; reject `to` > today.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the path and it holds. In KpiService.java line 134 the denominator is the whole calendar period: `long periodDays = Math.max(1, ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(from, to) + 1);`. Velocity is then `netUnits.divide(BigDecimal.valueOf(periodDays), ...)` and days of stock is `stock.divide(velocity, 1, HALF_UP)`. Nothing caps `to` at today or at the last sale date. `daysWithSales` is computed, but it only adds LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE when it is below 14. It is never used as the denominator and never compared with periodDays.

ReportCommand (lines 33-34) runs `LocalDate.parse` on --from and --to and does no range check, so a `to` date in the future is accepted.

RecommendationEngine line 37 raises RESTOCK only when `daysOfStock < restockBelowDays`, and RecommendationSettings.defaults() sets that to 14.

Finding's example: from=10-01, to=10-31, sales through 10-08, 16 units sold, 20 on hand. periodDays=31, velocity=16/31=0.516 (shown to 3 decimals), daysOfStock=20/0.516≈38.8 (the finding says 38.7, a tiny rounding slip). 38.8 is not below 14, so no RESTOCK. The real cover is 20/2=10 days, which would trigger RESTOCK. With the default slowMoverDays=90 this case does not become a slow mover, but other inputs can.

The staleness check doesn't catch a source gap either. RecommendationService takes dataAsOf as `max(ingested_at)` from import_batches, which is the import time, not the last sale date the data covers. So an export imported recently whose sales stop on 09-19 is not marked stale. It keeps HIGH confidence, or MEDIUM only if daysWithSales < 14, and a SLOW_MOVER can come out HIGH/PUBLISHABLE.

The README says "net units per day over the period", so dividing by the period is documented. But nothing documents or guards against a period that runs past today or past the data, and the founder's section 6 (line 90) requires a 'source gap' data-quality check. The understated velocity can hide RESTOCK and inflate slow movers, so the finding is confirmed at medium severity.

I could not refute this. The bug is reachable through the pilot CLI that the runbook tells people to use.

**The code**
- KpiService.java:134 sets `periodDays = DAYS.between(from, to) + 1`.
- Line 146 computes velocity as `netUnits / periodDays`.
- Line 153 computes `daysOfStock = stock / velocity`.
- Nothing limits the period to today or to the last sales date. `daysWithSales` is used only for the LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE flag at lines 135 and 158, never as the denominator.

**How real usage gets there**
- ReportCommand.run parses `--from` and `--to` with `LocalDate.parse` and does no further checks.
- WeeklyReportService.generate and RecommendationService.generate pass the dates straight to `KpiService.compute`. No caller rejects a `to` later than today or a `to` past where the data ends.
- A weekly or month-to-date run with the calendar period end (for example `--from=2026-10-01 --to=2026-10-31` on 2026-10-09) is a natural operator input, and nothing stops it.

**The worked example checks out**
- 16 units / 31 days = 0.5161 units per day. 20 / 0.5161 = 38.7 days of stock.
- RecommendationEngine:38 issues RESTOCK only when days of stock < `restockBelowDays`, which defaults to 14 (RecommendationSettings). So RESTOCK is suppressed.
- With the right denominator (2 per day) days of stock is 10, and RESTOCK would fire.

**Nothing else catches it**
- The staleness check uses `max(import_batches.ingested_at)`, the import time, not the date range the imported sales cover. A fresh import of data ending 10-08 is not flagged stale.
- LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE only lowers confidence to MEDIUM (`build()`). It does not bring back a RESTOCK that was never created.
- Nothing compares the dates the sales data covers with the requested period. Founder section 6 lists "source gap" as a required data-quality check, and section 7 says velocity must come from the relevant period.

**Documentation**
- README says "÷ net units per day over the period", and the vault deliberately does not exclude stockout days.
- That documents calendar days within a period that has already happened. It does not document counting future days, or days after the data ends, as zero-sales days.
- The future-`to` case is an unguarded input that clearly understates velocity. The source-gap case (data ending before a past `to`) is more arguable under the README wording, but the founder's source-gap requirement is not met.

Medium severity fits: it gives misleading restock and slow-mover advice, with no crash and no data loss.

I confirmed this from the code. In KpiService.java:134, `periodDays = DAYS.between(from, to) + 1` has no clamp. Velocity is `netUnits / periodDays` (line 148) and daysOfStock is `stock / velocity`. Neither `to` nor `from` is checked against today: ReportCommand only calls LocalDate.parse. Nothing compares the period with the last date that has sales. The only freshness check, in RecommendationService/RecommendationEngine, uses `max(import_batches.ingested_at)`, which is when the import ran, not the last date the data covers. So a file exported through 09-19 and imported yesterday counts as fresh. A grep finds no source-gap or coverage flag in KpiFlags or anywhere else.

Scenario 1: period 10-01..10-31, run on 10-09, 16 units sold in 8 days, 20 on hand. Velocity = 16/31 = 0.516 and daysOfStock = 38.8, which is above restockBelowDays = 14 (RecommendationSettings.defaults), so no RESTOCK is generated. The correct value is 10 days, which would trigger one. LOW_VELOCITY_SAMPLE is set because there are fewer than 14 sales days, but it only lowers confidence on recommendations that already exist. It cannot bring back the suppressed RESTOCK.

Scenario 2: September with sales only through 09-19. daysWithSales = 19, which is at least 14, so there is no LOW_VELOCITY flag. The data is not stale by ingestion date, so velocity is 37% too low at HIGH confidence. That can produce a false SLOW_MOVER, or hide a RESTOCK.

Is it intended? README says days of stock = "net units per day over the period", so dividing by the calendar period is documented. The KPI notes ("KPI и формулы.md") consciously leave out only stockout-day exclusion. Nothing documents ignoring source gaps or periods that end in the future. The founder doc lists "source gap" as a required data-quality check in section 6. Section 11 says a recommendation must not be published as reliable when the source is stale. Taking freshness from ingestion time and ignoring coverage contradicts that. The runbook also calls this a weekly report while its example uses a month-long period, so running mid-period with `to` at month end is a realistic mistake.

Medium is right: the result is a wrong restock or slow-mover signal with no warning, but no data is lost.

confirmed.title: Two unrelated payments with the same amount are marked MATCHED internal transfers
confirmed.description: Mirrored-pair detection pairs any debit on account A with any credit of the same amount on account B within the window, without checking currency, description or counterparty. The result is stored as MATCHED, both legs get is_internal_transfer=true, the report says they are 'not counted as income or expense', and the credit is dropped from acquiring matching. This contradicts decision #12 ('do not present weak evidence as strong').
confirmed.failure_scenario: On 2026-09-10 the shop pays 500,000 AMD rent from its Ameria account and a B2B customer pays 500,000 AMD into its Ardshin account. Both are reported as an internal transfer and the customer payment disappears from income. If an acquiring settlement equals a supplier payment, that card-sales day is reported as 'card sales without settlement'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Require the same currency plus a transfer marker or own-account evidence for MATCHED; report amount-only pairs as PLAUSIBLE without setting is_internal_transfer.

verdicts.reasoning:
The code path behaves as the finding says. In ReconciliationService.reconcile (lines 56-73), a pair is accepted on three checks only: the signs are opposite (lines 57/59), the accounts differ (`if (credit.accountRef.equals(debit.accountRef)) continue;`, line 60), the amounts are equal (`if (credit.amount.compareTo(debit.amount.negate()) != 0) continue;`, line 61), and the dates are at most transferWindowDays apart (line 62; the default is 1 in ReconciliationSettings.defaults()). Nothing checks currency (bank_transactions.currency exists, V2 line 104), description, counterparty or the 'acquiring' tag. The first credit that qualifies is taken (`break`, line 72). It is then stored as `new ReconLine("INTERNAL_TRANSFER_PAIR", "MATCHED", "MIRRORED_AMOUNT", ...)` (line 66), and markInternal sets `is_internal_transfer = true, internal_transfer_reason = 'mirrored_pair'` on both legs (lines 186-190). After that, line 95 (`if (t.amount.signum() <= 0 || paired.contains(t.id) || ...) continue;`) drops the paired credit from acquiring matching even when it carries the 'acquiring' tag. The day it would have settled then goes into the "card sales without settlement" list (lines 130-138). The weekly report (WeeklyReportService line 252) labels these pairs "Ներքին փոխանցումներ (սեփական հաշիվների միջև)" with the note "Չեն հաշվվում որպես եկամուտ կամ ծախս" ("internal transfers between own accounts, not counted as income or expense"). So in the scenario (500,000 AMD rent paid from account A, 500,000 AMD customer payment into account B on the same day), the reconciliation sheet does report a MATCHED internal transfer.

Mitigating points:
(1) The amount-only heuristic is documented in README lines 77-78 ("mirrored pairs (debit on account A = credit on account B within 1 day) are found at reconcile time. Both legs get is_internal_transfer = true"). The headline behaviour is therefore intended. Decision #12 covers acquiring without a payment method, not transfers, and the section 11 criterion (own-account transfers must not become double income/expense) is met, not broken.
(2) The claim that the customer payment "disappears from income" is overstated. No KPI, cash or report code reads is_internal_transfer; grep finds it only in CommitService's insert and in ReconciliationService. The harm is limited to the reconciliation sheet's counts and labels.

What remains a concrete, undocumented defect: there is no currency check, and acquiring-tagged credits are not excluded from pairing. A coincidental exact amount match within ±1 day therefore removes a real acquiring settlement from matching and produces a false SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT line, while the pair is shown with MATCHED certainty. Exact cent-level matches against acquiring settlements are rare. Round B2B amounts are more plausible but still need a coincidence within one day. I keep the finding but lower it to low severity.

I could not refute this. Normal usage reaches it.

**How it is reached**
- `WeeklyReportService:72` calls `reconcile()` on every weekly report run (`--report.run`), using `ReconciliationSettings.defaults()` with a 1-day window.
- `loadBank` loads every `bank_transactions` row for the tenant in the window, across all accounts.
- The pair loop (`ReconciliationService.java:56-74`) checks only four things: the amounts have opposite signs, the accounts differ (`accountRef`), the amounts are equal, and the dates are within the window.
- It does not check currency (the `currency` column exists in V2 but is never loaded), description, tags (a debit tagged `rent` is still eligible), or counterparty. No database constraint prevents this.
- It is greedy: it takes the first matching credit and breaks.

**The scenario is realistic.** A pilot tenant with two imported accounts (the runbook step 1b expects several own accounts) pays a round 500,000 AMD rent from Ameria. A customer pays 500,000 AMD into Ardshin on the same or the next day. Round AMD amounts are common.

**What happens**
- `markInternal` sets `is_internal_transfer=true` and `reason='mirrored_pair'` on both legs.
- A line `INTERNAL_TRANSFER_PAIR / MATCHED / MIRRORED_AMOUNT` is stored and shown on the «Համադրում» sheet. That sheet says the transfers are not counted as income or expense (`WeeklyReportService:252`), and `internalTransferAmount` goes up.
- Step 2 skips any credit in `paired` (line 95). If the captured credit is an acquiring settlement, it is never matched to a sales day. Step 3 then wrongly reports that day as `SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT`. This part needs an exact amount match with a non-round settlement, so it is rarer but still possible.
- The existing test `mirroredTransferBetweenOwnAccounts` only works because no 300000 credit happens to sit on another account near T3. One unrelated credit of that amount would turn T3 ("Supplier payment") into an internal transfer.

**What is overstated**
1. "The customer payment disappears from income": nothing in the main code reads `is_internal_transfer` for a bank-based income figure. I grepped: only CommitService writes it and only the recon code reads it. `CashPositionService` uses balances, not the flag. The harm is a misleading reconciliation sheet and a skipped acquiring match, not a wrong income KPI number.
2. The amount-only mirrored-pair rule is documented in the README ("debit on account A = credit on account B within 1 day"), so it is partly intended design. Decision #12 only covers acquiring without a payment method. What does conflict with the founder's requirements is labelling this weak evidence MATCHED: section 1 asks every finding to show its confidence level, and section 11 asks for correct currency handling, while this rule ignores currency.

Because the trigger is reachable but the main impact is a misleading reconciliation sheet rather than lost money or KPI data, I would lower the severity to low or medium.

The code matches the finding. In ReconciliationService.java (lines 56-73), a debit is paired with a credit when only three things hold: the account_ref differs, the absolute amounts are equal, and the dates are within transferWindowDays. Nothing checks currency (bank_transactions.currency is NOT NULL in V2 but loadBank never selects it), description, counterparty or the 'acquiring' tag. The pair is stored as status MATCHED with method MIRRORED_AMOUNT. markInternal sets is_internal_transfer=true on both legs. The paired credit is then skipped by the acquiring loop (line 95: paired.contains(t.id) → continue).

Is it intended? Partly. README lines 76-78 do document "mirrored pairs (debit on account A = credit on account B within 1 day)", so amount-only pairing between the client's own imported accounts is a documented heuristic. That alone would not make it a defect. Three parts are not documented and conflict with the founder doc and the decision log:
(1) Currency is ignored. A 500,000 AMD debit pairs with a 500,000 USD credit. Founder §11 acceptance criterion: "returns, discount, VAT, currency, rounding ... are handled correctly".
(2) A credit tagged 'acquiring' can be taken by the transfer pass before the acquiring pass runs. The real settlement then vanishes from matching, and if payment_method is mapped, that card-sales day shows as SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT. The report then falsely says "card sales with no acquiring credit found". That is a misleading report.
(3) An amount-only coincidence is reported as MATCHED. In WeeklyReportService.java line 252 the report labels it an own-account transfer "not counted as income or expense". Decision #12 ("do not present weak evidence as strong") rules this out, and the same file already uses PLAUSIBLE for the analogous weak acquiring evidence.

The scenario is realistic. Pilot shops have several accounts, and round B2B or rent amounts are common.

Severity correction within medium: the finding says the customer payment "disappears from income", but that part is overstated. No KPI currently reads is_internal_transfer (grep shows it is only written), so cash KPIs do not lose the amount today. The real harm is the misleading reconciliation sheet: a false internal transfer, a lost acquiring match and a false "sales without settlement" flag. Medium is appropriate.

confirmed.title: Contribution margin subtracts all costs from a partial gross profit, with no warning
confirmed.description: contribution = grossProfit (lines with COGS only) - variable cost x all sale lines - all ad spend. When COGS coverage is below 100%, the result mixes a partial base with full costs. The summary note ('gross profit - variable cost - ads') and the COGS_MISSING text ('gross profit is partial') never say that contribution is understated.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Net sales 1,000,000, COGS coverage 30% (GP 90,000 on the covered part), ad spend 200,000. The summary shows contribution -110,000, implying the shop loses money after ads when the real figure may be positive; the owner may cut profitable advertising.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Show contribution as unavailable or partial when cogsCoverage < 1 (or scale costs to the covered share), with an explicit 'contribution is partial' flag.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code path and the defect is real. The finding stands.

**How the numbers are built, in KpiService.java:**
- Gross profit only covers lines that have COGS. Line 117: `if (hasCogs) { acc.cogs = ...; acc.netSalesWithCogs = ...; acc.anyCogs = true; }`. Line 142: `if (a.anyCogs) { cogsTotal = cogsTotal.add(a.cogs); netWithCogs = netWithCogs.add(a.netSalesWithCogs); }`. Line 163: `BigDecimal grossProfit = netWithCogs.subtract(cogsTotal);`.
- Variable costs use every sale line, whether or not it has COGS. Line 124 counts `saleLines += lines;` for all non-return groups. Line 166: `BigDecimal variableCosts = settings.variableCostPerOrder().multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(saleLines));`.
- Ad spend is the full period total. Line 76: `SELECT coalesce(sum(spend), 0) FROM campaign_daily WHERE date BETWEEN :from AND :to`.
- Line 169 then computes `BigDecimal contribution = grossProfit.subtract(variableCosts).subtract(spend);`. No branch looks at `coverage` or `COGS_MISSING`: there is no scaling, no null and no contribution-specific flag. So with 30% coverage the result is 30%-based gross profit minus 100%-based costs.

**What the report shows.** WeeklyReportService.java:128 prints `money(s, st, r++, "Ծածկույթ (contribution)", k.contribution(), "Համախառն շահույթ − փոփոխական ծախս − գովազդ")`. That is a single number with the note "gross profit − variable cost − ads" and no partial marker. The only related text is ReportLabels.java:22 for COGS_MISSING: "Որոշ ապրանքների ինքնարժեքը բացակայում է. համախառն շահույթը մասնակի է" ("some products' cost is missing; gross profit is partial"). It says nothing about contribution. KpiFlags.java:7 likewise says only "gross profit covers only part of sales". RecommendationEngine never reads contribution, so nothing else adds a caveat.

**The finding's scenario holds.** Net sales 1,000,000 at 30% coverage gives netWithCogs of 300,000 and gross profit of 90,000. Subtracting 200,000 of ads gives -110,000, and variable costs for all sale lines push it lower still. The shop could be profitable on the full base, so the figure overstates the loss.

**Is it documented, intended behaviour?** Only in part. README lines 53-55 give the formula literally ("GP only over lines that have COGS", "Contribution = GP − ..."). But the class Javadoc (lines 18-20) promises "when an input is missing the figure is null or flagged, never guessed". Contribution is neither null nor flagged as partial. The founder's section 7 defines contribution as gross profit (net sales − COGS) − variable costs − ads, all on one base; mixing bases is not that KPI. Section 11 also requires that nothing be presented as reliable when COGS is missing.

**What softens it.** The COGS coverage % row and the generic COGS_MISSING flag do appear on the same sheet, so a careful reader could work out the caveat. That keeps the severity at medium rather than higher.

I could not refute this. Real imports reach it, and the code does what the finding says.

**Reachability.** `cogs_amount` is optional on import. In CommitService.java:104-111 a missing value only raises a `no_cogs` warning and the line is stored with `cogs_amount` NULL. The founder's scenario (section 3) lists cost as just one of several columns to map, and many POS exports have no cost column. So mixed or low COGS coverage is a normal state, not an impossible one.

**Computation** (KpiService.java):
- `grossProfit` is `netWithCogs - cogsTotal`, built only from groups where `has_cogs` is true.
- `variableCosts` is `variableCostPerOrder` × `saleLines`, counting every sale line, including lines with no COGS.
- `spend` is all of the `campaign_daily` spend for the period.
- Line 169: `contribution = grossProfit - variableCosts - spend`. A partial gross profit has full costs taken off it, and nothing in the code scales the costs, nulls the result or flags it.

**Presentation** (WeeklyReportService.java:128). The contribution row shows a plain number with the note "Gross profit − variable cost − advertising". The COGS_MISSING label in ReportLabels.java:22 says only that gross profit is partial; it never says contribution is understated. KpiReport.java:12 and README.md:55 document the formula but say nothing about coverage below 100%. So this is not documented-intended behaviour that would excuse it.

**Failure scenario.** Net sales 1,000,000, COGS coverage 30%, gross profit 90,000, ad spend 200,000. The summary shows contribution of about −110,000 minus variable costs, which looks like a loss after advertising even when the business is profitable.

**What softens it.** The COGS coverage % row sits two rows above contribution, and the COGS_MISSING flag appears in the data-reliability block. A careful reader could work out that contribution is affected. RecommendationEngine does not use `contribution`; its AD_TEST rule works from per-SKU margins. So the harm is limited to the human-facing report and is not amplified by automated advice. I'm keeping the severity at medium rather than raising it.

I could not refute this. The code behaves as the finding says, and no document treats the result as intended.

What the code does: KpiService.java:166-169 computes grossProfit as netWithCogs - cogsTotal, which only counts lines that have COGS. It then computes contribution = grossProfit - variableCostPerOrder*saleLines - spend. The variable cost uses every sale line (saleLines also counts lines without COGS), and spend is all ad spend for the period. So the uncovered sales add zero gross profit but still carry their full share of costs. This pushes contribution down every time, and the effect is not random. At 0% coverage, contribution is simply -(variable costs + ads) and is shown as a real figure. There is no partial or null handling and no flag tied to contribution. KpiFlags has none: COGS_MISSING says 'gross profit covers only part of sales', and NO_MARKETING_DATA is the only flag about contribution.

What the docs say:
- The README and KpiReport javadoc describe the two formulas separately: gross profit is computed only over lines with COGS, and contribution = GP - variable costs - ads. Neither says contribution is partial or understated when coverage is below 100%.
- The decision log (Решения.md) has nothing on contribution or how missing COGS should affect it.
- The founder doc (section 7) defines contribution from full gross profit (net sales - actual COGS), not from gross profit over the covered part only.
- The class's own rule, 'when an input is missing the figure is null or flagged, never guessed', is only met indirectly. In WeeklyReportService.java:128 the summary note reads 'Gross profit - variable cost - ads', and the COGS_MISSING label in ReportLabels.java:22 only says gross profit is partial.

So the formula is documented, but showing a contribution that mixes a covered base with full costs is not documented as intended. It also goes against the 'flag, never guess' principle and against how the founder defines contribution. The vault note 'AI-ассистенты и границы' rule 5 (ROAS high but contribution negative -> point out the contradiction) means this understated number could later produce false contradictions. Today nothing reads k.contribution() except the XLSX summary. Tests (KpiServiceIT:129) only cover contribution at 100% coverage.

What softens it: the COGS coverage % is printed two rows above, and the COGS_MISSING warning appears in the flags section. A careful reader could work it out, but the headline number itself is presented as definite.

Severity: medium is about right, perhaps toward the low end because of those cues. It misleads on the headline profit figure in the owner's report, but it causes no data loss or crash.

confirmed.title: VAT_UNKNOWN downgrade of AD_TEST (LOW/NEEDS_DATA/vat_basis) and the FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED rule are never asserted
confirmed.description: vatUnknownOrCogsMissing_... produces [RESTOCK A-1, AD_TEST A-1 (NEEDS_DATA, LOW, missing vat_basis), ASK_ACCOUNTANT] but only asserts the size and the ASK's missing list. No other test produces an AD_TEST under VAT_UNKNOWN (RecommendationServiceIT uses vat_included=false, WeeklyReportServiceIT has VAT confirmed). The FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED -> MEDIUM rule is not asserted either.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Delete RecommendationEngine lines 103-108. AD_TEST is then published HIGH/PUBLISHABLE with max_acquisition_cost computed from VAT-inclusive prices treated as net, overstating the allowed acquisition cost by about 20%, and every test stays green.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Assert find(recs, AD_TEST) has status NEEDS_DATA, confidence LOW and missing containing vat_basis; add a FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED case expecting MEDIUM.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code and the finding holds. It is a test-coverage gap, not a defect in the production code.

**What the test actually produces.** In RecommendationEngineTest line 81, the report carries the VAT_UNKNOWN flag and the default settings apply. RecommendationSettings.defaults() is (14, 14, 3), so at most 3 recommendations are kept.
- **RESTOCK for A-1:** A-1 has 5.0 days of stock, below 14, so a RESTOCK is built at priority 1.
- **No RESTOCK for B-1 or D-1:** their days of stock are 378.4 and 3000.
- **SLOW_MOVER for D-1:** D-1 is flagged as a slow mover, so it gets one at priority 3.
- **AD_TEST for A-1:** all three SKUs pass the AD_TEST check (margins 11000, 11000 and 8000). The engine keeps the SKU with the highest grossProfit, and A-1 has 780000, against 130000 for B-1 and 30000 for D-1. So AD_TEST is built for A-1 at priority 2.

After sorting, the list is [RESTOCK, AD_TEST, SLOW_MOVER]. Because the accountant question is critical here (line 87, `else if (criticalAsk) out.set(out.size() - 1, ask);`), it replaces SLOW_MOVER. The final list is [RESTOCK A-1, AD_TEST A-1, ASK_ACCOUNTANT], as the finding says.

Inside build(), lines 104-108 (`if (k.flags().contains(KpiFlags.VAT_UNKNOWN)) { c = Confidence.LOW; status = Recommendation.Status.NEEDS_DATA; miss.add("vat_basis"); }`) set the AD_TEST to LOW and NEEDS_DATA and add vat_basis to its missing list.

**What the test checks.** Lines 83-85 only check that there are 3 items, that an ASK_ACCOUNTANT exists, and that the ASK's missing list contains vat_basis. The ASK gets vat_basis from accountantQuestion() at line 121, not from lines 104-108. So deleting lines 103-108 leaves this test green.

**No other test covers these rules.**
- **RecommendationServiceIT:** its sale lines use vat_included=false, so VAT is known. It checks only the AD_TEST's max_acquisition_cost and assumptions, never its confidence or status. Its stale-data test gets NEEDS_DATA from the stale branch (lines 110-113), not the VAT branch.
- **WeeklyReportServiceIT:** VAT is confirmed there (line 85 asserts VAT_UNKNOWN is absent). It only checks that the word "Վստահություն" (confidence) appears.
- **ClaudePayloadTest, ExplanationGuardTest, TemplateExplanationTest:** they build Recommendation objects by hand and never run the engine.
- **RecommendationEngineTest line 109 (FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED):** it passes an empty SKU list, so no AD_TEST is produced and the MEDIUM downgrade on line 103 never runs.

So both rules can be deleted without any test failing.

**Severity.** I'd lower it to low. Nothing is wrong today, and the scenario needs someone to delete the guard first. Also, the "overstating by 20%" part goes a bit beyond the code: the facts are computed the same way either way, and the guard only changes the label to LOW / NEEDS_DATA. Losing it would still mean ad advice is published as HIGH / PUBLISHABLE while the VAT basis is unknown. The coverage gap itself is real.

I confirmed the test gap, and the code it fails to protect runs on real data.

1. The test at line 83 really produces an AD_TEST under VAT_UNKNOWN and never checks it. The default settings are (14, 14, 3), so at most 3 recommendations. The candidates are RESTOCK A-1 (priority 1), AD_TEST (priority 2) and SLOW_MOVER D-1 (priority 3). A-1 wins AD_TEST because it has the highest gross profit: 780000, against 130000 for B-1 and 30000 for D-1. ASK_ACCOUNTANT is critical, so it takes the last slot from SLOW_MOVER. The output is therefore [RESTOCK, AD_TEST A-1, ASK]. The test checks only the list size, that an ASK is present, and that the ASK's missing list contains vat_basis.

2. No other test checks the AD_TEST downgrade:
   - grep finds `vat_basis` only in the ASK assertion.
   - The only NEEDS_DATA assertions are for stale data: engine test line 96 and RecommendationServiceIT line 112. Neither involves VAT.
   - RecommendationServiceIT inserts rows with vat_included=false.
   - WeeklyReportServiceIT asserts VAT_UNKNOWN is absent.
   - No test checks MEDIUM confidence for AD_TEST under FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED. The only MEDIUM assertion is the RESTOCK LOW_VELOCITY case. RecommendationServiceIT probably runs with FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED set, but it never checks confidence.

   So deleting RecommendationEngine lines 103-108 would leave every test green.

3. Real usage reaches the guarded code:
   - The `sale_lines.vat_included` column allows NULL (V2 migration, line 51, "NULL = unknown").
   - `MappingSettings.vatIncluded` may be null.
   - CommitService lines 107-108 only add a warning (`vat_unknown`) and still commit the row with a NULL `vat_included`.
   - KpiService lines 106-109 then set VAT_UNKNOWN and leave the gross amount as net, with no VAT correction.
   - FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED is the default whenever the formulas are not confirmed (KpiService line 37).

   So the regression described is realistic: an AD_TEST would be shown HIGH and PUBLISHABLE, with max_acquisition_cost inflated by VAT-inclusive prices.

One correction to the finding: if prices do include 20% VAT, the inflation is more than 20%. The ~20% overstatement applies to the net price per unit, and the unchanged costs are then subtracted from it.

On severity: production code is correct today. This is a missing regression check on behaviour the acceptance criteria call for, not a live bug, so low is the better rating.

I could not refute this. It is a real test gap, not documented behavior.

Code: RecommendationEngine.build() lines 102-108 are the only place AD_TEST is downgraded. FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED with HIGH confidence becomes MEDIUM. VAT_UNKNOWN becomes LOW, NEEDS_DATA and adds "vat_basis" to missing.

Tests: RecommendationEngineTest.vatUnknownOrCogsMissing_... (lines 77-86) gives the VAT_UNKNOWN report-level flag to SKUs that do produce an AD_TEST (B-1 has the highest gross profit and positive margin). It only asserts hasSize(3), that an ASK_ACCOUNTANT is present, and that its missing list contains vat_basis. It never looks at the AD_TEST's confidence, status or missing list. A grep of src/test finds no other assertion on AD_TEST confidence or status:
- RecommendationServiceIT inserts vat_included=false and builds KpiSettings with formulasConfirmed=false. It checks only max_acquisition_cost and assumptions, never confidence.
- WeeklyReportServiceIT has VAT confirmed.
- ClaudePayloadTest, ExplanationGuardTest and TemplateExplanationTest build Recommendation objects by hand.
- noSalesData_... uses FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED with no SKUs, so no AD_TEST is built.

Intent: nothing in the docs says this downgrade may go untested. README lines 51-52 say vat_included=NULL is computed as-is and flagged VAT_UNKNOWN, which means the downgrade is the only guard. Founder doc §11 line 146 requires VAT to be handled correctly. Line 147 says a recommendation must not be published as trustworthy when the data is unreliable. Line 17 says every recommendation must show its confidence level. A regression here would publish a HIGH/PUBLISHABLE max_acquisition_cost computed from prices that may include VAT. With the test's numbers, 35,000 net per unit could really be 42,000 gross, so the overstatement of the margin is far more than 20%. The finding's "about 20%" applies to the price, not the margin.

confirmed.title: TenantIsolationIT's 'no tenant set => no rows' check cannot detect a session-scoped tenant leak
confirmed.description: seenWithoutTenant runs right after tenantTx.inTenant(b, ...), and tenant B is empty. HikariCP hands the same thread its most recently returned connection, so if TenantTransactions switched set_config('app.tenant_id', :tenant, false) to session scope (line 29), the unscoped query would run with app.tenant_id = B and still count 0. No other test queries outside inTenant, so the README guarantee ('outside such a transaction the variable is NULL') is unprotected.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Change `true` to `false` in TenantTransactions.inTenant. app.tenant_id persists on pooled connections and any code path querying outside inTenant sees the previous request's tenant data; TenantIsolationIT still passes because the leaked tenant is the empty B.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Run the unscoped count after an inTenant(a, ...) call (A has rows), and assert current_setting('app.tenant_id', true) is NULL/empty outside inTenant.

verdicts.reasoning:
I confirmed the code path. The weakness is real, but it is a gap in test coverage, not a live defect, so I rate it low rather than medium.

The code path in TenantIsolationIT, lines 35-41:
- Line 35: `seenByA = tenantTx.inTenant(a, ...)`
- Line 36: `seenByB = tenantTx.inTenant(b, ...)`. Tenant B has no rows.
- Line 37: `seenWithoutTenant = jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM source_records")...`, run outside any transaction, right after the B call.
- Line 41: `assertThat(seenWithoutTenant).isZero()`

TenantTransactions.java line 29 runs `SELECT set_config('app.tenant_id', :tenant, true)`. Its javadoc (lines 11-14) promises "Outside of it the variable is NULL and RLS returns nothing." The RLS policies (V1:69-76, V2:133, V3:49) are `tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid`.

Suppose someone changes `true` to `false` on line 29. The setting then lives on the session and survives the commit. HikariCP's ConcurrentBag looks first at the connections this thread returned, starting with the most recent one, so line 37 almost certainly gets the same connection line 36 just used. That connection still has app.tenant_id = B, and B has zero source_records, so the count is 0 and the test passes. The leaked tenant is never A, the one with 4 rows.

No other test checks this. I searched src/test for jdbc.sql calls outside inTenant: the only other ones insert rows into tenants. Nothing reads current_setting outside a transaction. The second test only checks WITH CHECK on writes inside inTenant(b).

Why low rather than medium:
- The current production code is correct. Line 29 uses `true`, so nothing leaks today.
- The failure only appears after a hypothetical regression.
- Every main-code query I sampled runs as `jdbc.sql` inside an inTenant lambda (CommitService, KpiService), and inTenant always sets the variable again at the start. Even with session scope, those paths would not see another tenant's data. Only code that queries outside inTenant would, and I found none in main.

So this test does not protect the documented NULL-outside-a-transaction guarantee, but nothing currently produces a wrong result.

I could not confirm this as a reachable defect. The failure scenario only happens if someone first changes the code: it needs TenantTransactions.inTenant (line 29) to be edited from set_config('app.tenant_id', :tenant, true) to false. The code as written uses is_local = true. The single set_config call in src/main is at TenantTransactions.java:29. V1 migration line 2 documents the same per-transaction contract. The RLS policies use NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so the table-owner app role is covered as well. In current code, app.tenant_id is reset when each transaction ends, so a pooled connection carries no tenant into later queries. That means no real input, CLI path or DB state produces a leak, wrong output or isolation breach.

What remains is a point about test strength. Because the test checks B, the empty tenant, last, it would not catch that hypothetical mutation. The analysis of how HikariCP reuses connections is plausible. Still, a gap in coverage against a regression that does not exist is the kind of "consider adding a test" note the task rules out. It is not a concrete defect with a failure path in the shipped code.

The mechanism holds up. TenantIsolationIT.java:35-37 runs the unscoped count straight after inTenant(b, ...), and tenant B has no rows. TenantTransactions.java:29 currently uses set_config('app.tenant_id', :tenant, true). README line 24 states the guarantee: "Outside such a transaction the variable is NULL and RLS returns no rows". On borrow, HikariCP's ConcurrentBag first checks the calling thread's own list of returned connections, newest first. So on a single test thread the unscoped JdbcClient query almost always reuses the same physical connection that inTenant(b) just returned. If someone flipped is_local to false, that connection would still carry app.tenant_id = B. The policy `tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting(...), '')::uuid` would then filter to B, which is empty, so the query returns 0 and assertThat(seenWithoutTenant).isZero() still passes. No other IT queries outside inTenant or checks current_setting outside a transaction (grep of src/test confirms this), so this regression would go unnoticed. Nothing in the README or decision log says the check is meant to be this weak. The test's javadoc says it covers the founder's tenant-isolation acceptance criterion, so its passing gives a misleading picture of coverage.

Severity should be low, not medium. The production code is correct today: is_local is true, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set, and the role is NOBYPASSRLS. No data leaks now. The finding is a test that would miss a specific hypothetical regression, not a live isolation breach or data loss. Simply reordering the asserts to run the unscoped count after inTenant(a), or asserting that current_setting is null outside a transaction, would close the gap.

confirmed.title: Shipped HC mapping uses a post-discount amount as gross_amount, so discounts are subtracted twice
confirmed.description: Target_Schema defines gross_amount as 'Line amount before discount', and KpiService:106 computes gross - discount. The runbook's mapping hc_sales_v1 maps gross_amount to 'Գումար (ԱԱՀ-ով)' and discount_amount to 'Զեղչ'. In the repository's own HC layout (the SYNTHETIC_HC_sales xlsx, also the test fixture), the amount column already has the discount deducted. Every one of the 63 discounted rows whose SKU has a known undiscounted price satisfies amount = list price x qty - discount. For example, Հ-00009 has 2 x 57,600 - 5,760 = 109,440. KpiService:106 and ReconciliationService.dailySales:173 deduct the discount again. The summary sheet still labels the figure 'զեղչից առաջ' (before discount) (WeeklyReportService:119).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A line of 2 x 48,000 incl. VAT carries a 4,800 discount and was paid 91,200. KPI net = (91,200 - 4,800)/1.2 = 72,000 instead of 76,000, an understatement of 4,000 (5.3%) on that line. September in the sample has 77,000 of discounts, so net sales and GP are understated by 64,167 AMD. Reconciliation card-sales days are short by the full discount, which inflates the implied acquiring fee and can push a day above 3% to UNMATCHED.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Map gross_amount to a pre-discount column or compute it as amount + discount. Alternatively, add a mapping setting 'amountIsNetOfDiscount' and skip the subtraction when it is set.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The code path behaves as the finding says, and the repo's own sample data shows the amount column already has the discount taken off.

**The mapping and the definition**
- In docs/samples/mappings/hc_sales_v1.json, line 14 maps `"gross_amount": "Գումար (ԱԱՀ-ով)"` and line 15 maps `"discount_amount": "Զեղչ"`.
- The column_mapping_template_v1.xlsx Target_Schema sheet defines gross_amount as `'Line amount before discount, in currency'`.

**The code subtracts the discount from it**
- KpiService.java:106 does `BigDecimal netGroup = gross.subtract(discount);` and then divides by 1.2 when VAT is included.
- ReconciliationService.java:173 computes `gross_amount - discount_amount` as the amount paid.
- WeeklyReportService.java:119 labels grossSales "զեղչից առաջ" (before discount).

**The sample data is already net of discount**
- I read SYNTHETIC_HC_sales_2026-07-01_2026-09-30.xlsx with openpyxl. Every SKU has one undiscounted unit price incl. VAT: A-1045 and A-1046 at 42000, B-2001 at 57600, C-3010 at 14400, D-4100 at 5400.
- All 76 discounted rows on those SKUs, with 0 exceptions, satisfy `Գումար (ԱԱՀ-ով) = unit price × qty − Զեղչ × 1.2`.
  - Հ-00009 (B-2001, qty 2, Զեղչ 4800): 115200 − 5760 = 109440.
  - Հ-00003 (A-1045, qty 2, Զեղչ 3500): 84000 − 4200 = 79800.
  - Հ-00005 (D-4100, qty 3, Զեղչ 450): 16200 − 540 = 15660.
- The "Գումար (առանց ԱԱՀ)" column is post-discount as well (Հ-00003: (70000 − 3500)/1.2 = 55417). So no column maps to a pre-discount amount.

When this file is imported with the shipped mapping, the discount is deducted once in the source data and again at KpiService:106 and ReconciliationService:173. Net sales and gross profit are understated by roughly the total discount. September discounts in the sample total 77,000, which matches the finding. The summary sheet still calls the gross figure "before discount", which misleads.

**Corrections to the finding's arithmetic**
- The Զեղչ column for Հ-00009 holds 4800, not 5760. The amount is list − 1.2 × discount, so the discount column looks like it is on a different VAT basis than the amount.
- The finding counts 63 discounted rows; I count 76.
- Neither point changes the conclusion that the amount is post-discount.

**Why I did not refute it**
- PILOT_RUNBOOK.md:25 says the sample headers are synthetic and must be replaced, and Backlog.md says the fixture will be replaced by a real ՀԾ export. That covers header names, not what the columns mean.
- Nothing in README, the decision log or the runbook says the HC amount column is pre-discount. Founder requirement §8 (line 96) wants net = sale amount − discount − return. The repo's own canonical layout plus the shipped mapping break that.
- PilotCliIT only checks row counts, so no test catches it.

**Uncertainty**
I lowered confidence to medium for two reasons. The real HC export's semantics are not known yet. Also, the test fixture copy (src/test/resources/fixtures/synthetic_hc_sales.xlsx) differs from the docs copy byte-for-byte; I did not check whether that is only zip metadata.

Real usage reaches this path. PILOT_RUNBOOK.md step 2 runs `--import.run` with `--mapping=../docs/samples/mappings/hc_sales_v1.json`. That mapping is byte-identical to the test fixture app/src/test/resources/fixtures/hc_sales_v1.json, and it maps gross_amount to 'Գումար (ԱԱՀ-ով)' and discount_amount to 'Զեղչ'. CommitServiceIT, WeeklyReportServiceIT and PilotCliIT use the same mapping. The test fixture synthetic_hc_sales.xlsx has the same cell data as docs/samples/SYNTHETIC_HC_sales_*.xlsx (314 rows, all equal).

I checked the shipped data with openpyxl. I took the per-unit price from undiscounted lines of the same SKU. For all 76 discounted sale lines where that price is known, the VAT-inclusive amount equals price x qty - discount x 1.2. So the amount column is already net of discount, and the Զեղչ column is ex-VAT. Example Հ-00009 (B-2001, unit price 57,600): 2 x 57,600 = 115,200, minus 4,800 x 1.2 = 109,440. That matches the file.

KpiService (lines ~106-111) computes netGroup = (gross - discount) / 1.2. ReconciliationService.dailySales computes paid = gross_amount - discount_amount. Both therefore deduct the discount a second time. WeeklyReportService also labels gross sales 'զեղչից առաջ' (before discount), which is not what the figure is.

The finding gets some details wrong. Its example says the discount is 5,760; the file says 4,800, ex-VAT. Its formula leaves out the x1.2 factor. Neither changes the conclusion: the amount is post-discount, so net is understated by discount/1.2 per line. September sale discounts in the file total 77,000, which gives the stated 64,167 AMD understatement of net sales and GP. Reconciliation daily card sales are short by the full discount.

Mitigating points. The README and the mapping name say the layout is synthetic and real HC semantics are unverified. The runbook tells operators to replace the headers, but says nothing about checking whether the amount column is before or after discount. As shipped, the repo's own data and its mapping/KPI pipeline disagree. The sample weekly report and the tests are built on that disagreement, and it misstates net sales against the founder's formula (sale amount - discount - returns).

I could not refute this. The core claim holds, and nothing in the docs says this is intended.

1. **The sample amounts already have the discount taken off.** In docs/samples/SYNTHETIC_HC_sales_2026-07-01_2026-09-30.xlsx (313 rows), the 'Գումար (առանց ԱԱՀ)' (amount excl. VAT) column equals qty × list price excl. VAT − Զեղչ (discount)/1.2 on every row, for every SKU. Adding back discount/1.2 gives one constant unit price per SKU: B-2001 40000, C-3010 10000, D-4100 3750, A-1045/A-1046 ~29167. Example: Հ-00211 is 1 × B-2001 with discount 4800 and excl amount 36000, and 40000 − 4800/1.2 = 36000.

2. **The incl-VAT column the mapping uses is also net of discount.** 'Գումար (ԱԱՀ-ով)' equals excl × 1.44 on sale rows (a separate generator quirk) and excl × 1.2 on returns. So the discount is gone from it too.

3. **The code subtracts the discount again.** hc_sales_v1.json (docs/samples/mappings and the test fixture copy) maps gross_amount to 'Գումար (ԱԱՀ-ով)' and discount_amount to 'Զեղչ'. KpiService computes netGroup = gross.subtract(discount), and ReconciliationService line 173 computes paid = gross_amount − discount_amount. Both take the discount off a second time.

4. **One detail in the finding is off.** For B-2001 the incl column drops by 5760 per discounted line, not the 4800 in the Զեղչ column, because of the 1.44 quirk. The direction and conclusion are unaffected.

5. **Not documented as intended.** README ('Net sales = gross − discounts − returns'), the KPI note and the founder doc §7 all define a pre-discount gross. None says the HC amount column is post-discount. The decision log has nothing on this.

6. **It conflicts with the founder acceptance criteria.** Founder doc §11 requires that discounts are handled correctly ('զեղչը ... ճիշտ են մշակվում'). The app's own model of an ArmSoft export puts post-discount amounts in this column. Pilot runbook step 1 tells operators to copy this mapping and replace only the headers, not to check what the amount column means. ColumnMapping has no setting for 'amount is net of discount', so a client export like this cannot be configured correctly. Net sales and GP then come out low by discount/1.2. Sales days in reconciliation come out low by the full discount, so the gap to the bank looks like a bigger fee.

**Mitigations, so medium is the upper bound.**
- The fixture and sample are labelled synthetic. The runbook and backlog say to re-check against a real ArmSoft export, whose semantics are unverified.
- FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED stays on the report until the accountant signs off, and the accountant checklist covers discounts.
- The sample data's own 1.44 VAT quirk already distorts the sample report.

Real impact depends on whether real HC exports are post-discount. The app's own model of that export says they are, which makes this a plausible pilot-time misstatement. Medium is defensible, though it borders on low.

- Row Հ-00003 (A-1045, qty 2, discount 3500): ex-VAT 55417 = (70000 − 3500) / 1.2, and with-VAT 79800 = 66500 × 1.2. The 35000 unit price already includes VAT.

- It shows gross 6,621,600, discounts 77,000, returns 72,916.67, net 5,380,916.67, COGS 3,365,800 and GP 2,015,116.67.

confirmed.title: MT940 rows use the :61: value date as occurred_at but carry a booking-order running balance, so back- or forward-valued lines give a wrong or missing cash balance
confirmed.description: The :61: regex captures the optional entry (booking) date in group 2 and then discards it. value_date, which the MT940 mapping uses as occurred_at, comes from group 1. balance_after, however, is the running balance in the file's booking order. CashPositionService takes the latest day by occurred_at and looks for the single line on that day whose balance is not another same-day line's 'balance before'. A line whose value date differs from its booking date moves to another day, out of its place in the balance chain. This affects weekend bookings, acquiring settlements, card holds, back-valued corrections or chargebacks, and forward-valued FX deals.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The statement contains :60F:C260928AMD1000000,00, then :61:2609300930D200000,00NTRFREF1 (value Sep 30, balance 800,000), then :61:2609290930C500000,00NTRFREF2 (value Sep 29, booked Sep 30, balance 1,300,000), then :62F:C260930AMD1300000,00. The file passes the closing-balance check. CashPositionService.asOf(Sep 30) takes only REF1 for the latest day and reports 800,000 AMD as the non-stale 'last known balance', while the bank's booked closing balance is 1,300,000. A report re-run for Sep 29 then finds two chain ends on that day, so a balance that was correct before becomes 'ambiguous_order' with no number.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Emit the entry date as a booking_date column, resolving its year from the value date and handling year rollover. Order and group the cash position by booking date, and keep value_date for the settlement-lag logic.

Line 74 is `cells.put("value_date", date(m.group(1)).toString());`, which stores only the value date. Line 71 (`s.running = s.running.add(signedAmt)`) and line 82 (`balance_after`) build the running balance in file order. Lines 93-105 check only that the final running total equals :62F:, so the stated file passes.

2. Mapping. The shipped mapping docs/samples/mappings/bank_mt940_v1.json (the same as the test fixture) maps `"occurred_at": "value_date"`. CommitService.bankTransaction then inserts occurred_at from that field. No booking date is stored anywhere.

3. Cash position. CashPositionService.asOf (lines 42-52) takes `max((occurred_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Yerevan')::date)` for each account and keeps only that day's lines. lastKnown (lines 80-88) chooses the single line whose balance_after is not another line's balance_after minus amount.

Tracing the stated input:
- :60F: opens at 1,000,000.
- REF1 parses to value 2026-09-30, amount -200,000, balance 800,000.
- REF2 parses to value 2026-09-29, amount +500,000, balance 1,300,000.
- :62F: is 1,300,000, which matches, so the file is accepted.

The secondary claim also holds. asOf(Sep 29) groups REF2 (before 800,000, after 1,300,000) with any earlier statement's Sep 29 lines. Those cannot link to REF2, so there can be two chain ends and the result becomes ambiguous_order.

Nothing in the README MT940 section or decision #13 says value-date grouping with a booking-order balance is intended. Decision #13 only covers the opening + lines = closing check. Statement lines with a value date different from the entry date (back-valued corrections, weekend bookings, acquiring settlements) are normal in MT940, so this is a realistic way to get a wrong "last known balance" shown as current. - **Mapping:** the documented mapping `docs/samples/mappings/bank_mt940_v1.json` maps `"occurred_at": "value_date"`. The parser emits no booking-date key, so a user cannot map around this.
