- **The README publishes the password.** `app/README.md` line 13 says `CREATE ROLE retail_app LOGIN PASSWORD 'retail_app' NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS;`. Lines 14-15 make that role the owner of `retail_dev` and `retail_test`. Line 19 only says "Override with DB_URL, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD."
- **The pilot procedure never sets the variable.** `docs/PILOT_RUNBOOK.md` line 6 defines `J="java -jar target/retail-ai-platform-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar ..."`, and the pilot cycle for a real client (tenant create, imports, report) runs through `$J`. No step sets `DB_PASSWORD`, and the runbook says nothing about secrets. So the documented pilot path really does connect with the published password, to the role that owns all tenant tables.
- **The role can switch off isolation.** RLS is forced: `ALTER TABLE %I FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` appears in migrations V2, V3 and V4. But the table owner can still run `ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE` or `DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, so anyone holding this password can read across tenants.
- **It conflicts with a founder requirement.** Section 9 of `docs/CLAUDE_RETAIL_AI_PLATFORM_CONTEXT_HY.md` (line 123) requires a secrets store (գաղտնիքների շտեմարան). The decision log does not document the fallback as an accepted exception; `vault/40-Архитектура/Варианты архитектуры.md` only mentions "Secrets: env + зашифрованная таблица credentials".

Severity stays low, with these caveats:
- The scenario of "anyone who can reach the DB port" depends on how the server is deployed. By default PostgreSQL listens only on localhost, and the runbook's default URL is `localhost:5432/retail_dev`. So remote exposure needs `listen_addresses` and `pg_hba.conf` to be opened as well.
- The README defaults are framed as setup for running tests locally.

Still, the defect is real and shows in the code: there is no fail-fast, and the documented pilot procedure runs production client data under a credential published in the repository.

The fallback itself is reachable. app/src/main/resources/application.yml:7 is `password: ${DB_PASSWORD:retail_app}`, and docs/PILOT_RUNBOOK.md runs `java -jar target/...jar` with no DB_* env, so the pilot does connect with 'retail_app'. The defect as claimed still does not hold up:

1. The weak password comes from the README, not from the yml fallback. app/README.md:13 tells operators to create the role with `PASSWORD 'retail_app'`, and README:19 says to override with DB_URL/DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD. If the fallback were removed as suggested, someone following the README would just set DB_PASSWORD=retail_app and the result would be the same. A fail-fast startup does not close the scenario described.

2. Both the README and the runbook describe the defaults as intended. The default URL even points at `localhost:5432/retail_dev`. The runbook (no UI, run from `app/` after `mvn package`) is a CLI on the operator's machine against a local Postgres. Nothing in the repo deploys a server, adds a systemd unit or opens the DB port. The harm ("anyone who can reach the DB port gets full access") needs the operator to expose Postgres beyond localhost in listen_addresses/pg_hba. That is infrastructure state outside this code, not something the code reaches.

3. No founder acceptance criterion is broken. Section 11 covers tenant users seeing each other's data through API/UI/AI. That is enforced by RLS with FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and a config default does not change it. Section 9 (vault "Варианты архитектуры") plans secrets in env, which this config already supports.

What is left is hardening advice ("fail fast when no secret is set"), not a concrete defect with a code-reachable failure path. At most it is a low-severity deployment hygiene note.

The code matches the finding. Line 7 of app/src/main/resources/application.yml reads `password: ${DB_PASSWORD:retail_app}`. Lines 5-6 also fall back to `retail_dev` and the `retail_app` user. There is no separate dev or test profile for these values. app/src/test/resources/application-test.yml exists, but main config has no profile, so a production jar runs with the same fallbacks.

Is it documented as intended? Only as a local test setup. README line 13 creates the role with PASSWORD 'retail_app' under the heading "Run tests locally", followed by "Override with DB_URL, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD." Nothing in the README, the decision log (vault/00-Index/Решения.md) or vault/40-Архитектура says production or pilot may use these defaults.

docs/PILOT_RUNBOOK.md, which handles real client data, runs `java -jar target/...jar` with no DB_PASSWORD or DB_URL. So a pilot set up exactly as written connects to retail_dev with the password published in the repo, and nothing warns about it.

This conflicts with the founder's section 9, which asks for a secrets store (գաղտնիքների շտեմարան), encryption and tenant isolation. It is not intended behavior that matches the founder's requirements.

The role is NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS, but it owns the tables and the database. An owner can ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE / DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Even without that, the app role can read every tenant by setting app.tenant_id itself, so the password gives access to all clients' data.

Why the severity stays low:
- Exploiting this needs network access to PostgreSQL. By default PostgreSQL listens on localhost and pg_hba limits access, and the runbook implies a single operator machine.
- Fail-fast alone would not fix the weak password. An operator following the README would still create the role with 'retail_app' and could just set DB_PASSWORD=retail_app.

This is a real hardening defect (a hard-coded, publicly known credential fallback with no fail-fast) whose impact depends on how the server is deployed. Low is the right severity.

confirmed.title: MT940 :86: hard-wrapped mid-word is rejoined with a space, so vocabulary tags (acquiring) are missed
confirmed.description: :86: lines are cut at 65 characters, often mid-word. Continuation lines are joined with '\n' and then replaced by ' '.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: ':86:Оплата услуг эквай\nринга за сентябрь' gives 'Оплата услуг эквай ринга ...' and tags [] instead of [acquiring]. The settlement is skipped in reconciliation and the day is reported as card sales without settlement.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For tagging, also match against the description with line joins removed, or try both joins.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The code path behaves exactly as the finding says.

1. In Mt940Parser.tokenize (line 129), a line that does not start a new tag is added to the previous field as `last[1] + "\n" + line.strip()`. So ':86:Оплата услуг эквай' followed by 'ринга за сентябрь' becomes the value "Оплата услуг эквай\nринга за сентябрь".
2. Mt940Parser line 90 turns that into the description with `value.replace("\n", " ").replaceAll("\\s+", " ").trim()`. The result is "Оплата услуг эквай ринга за сентябрь", with a space inside the word.
3. CommitService line 249 tags this joined text: `BankDescriptionTagger.tags(r.text("description"))`. In BankDescriptionTagger, "эквайринг" is longer than 4 characters, so it is matched with `text.contains(term)`. That fails on "эквай ринга". No other word in the acquiring list ("pos", "acquiring", "card settlement", ...) is in the text, so no tags come back.
4. In ReconciliationService line 96, `if (!t.tags.contains("acquiring")) continue;` skips the credit. Because nothing claims that sales day, it is reported as SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT (lines 130-137) when card payment methods exist.
5. This cannot be fixed after the import. ReconciliationSettings says tags are set only at commit time, and the stored description is masked (`maskDescription`).

The authors did handle line wraps elsewhere. Own-account detection at CommitService line 238 removes whitespace with `.replaceAll("[\\s-]", "")`. Tag matching gets no such treatment.

How likely it is: SWIFT :86: is up to 6 lines of 65 characters, and many CIS-region banks cut at the column limit without regard to word breaks. The finding's own example is not realistic, because it breaks after 22 characters. A realistic case is a cut at column 65 that falls inside 'эквайринг', 'էքվայրինգ' or 'acquiring'. The README says the :86: wording of Armenian banks is UNVERIFIED, so this behaviour is not documented as intended.

The impact is narrow. The cut has to land inside a vocabulary word, and the line must contain no other matching word such as 'POS'. Low severity is appropriate.

Real use reaches this code. The documented CLI import (PILOT_RUNBOOK: `--file=*.sta --mapping=bank_mt940_v1.json`) runs Mt940Parser. `tokenize()` (lines 119-131) adds each continuation line to the previous field with "\n". At line 90, the `:86:` handler turns "\n" into " " and collapses runs of whitespace. The mapping sends the `description` cell straight to `description`. CommitService.java:249 then calls `BankDescriptionTagger.tags(r.text("description"))` on that space-joined text. The tags are stored as `description_tags`. ReconciliationService.java:96 only looks at credits tagged `acquiring`. ReconciliationSettings says the stored description is masked, so the tags cannot be worked out again later.

For terms longer than 4 characters, the tagger uses plain `text.contains(term)`, so "эквай ринга" does not match "эквайринг". The same goes for "էքվայ րինգ" and "acqui ring". The credit gets no `acquiring` tag. That gives two wrong reconciliation lines: it is never matched as an ACQUIRING_SETTLEMENT, and the card-sales day can show up as SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT.

The input is realistic. SWIFT limits `:86:` to 6 lines of 65 characters, and many banks wrap it mechanically at 65 characters, mid-word. Nothing (DB constraint, mapping setting or parser option) stops this or normalises it. Own-account detection (CommitService ~237) strips all whitespace before matching, so it is not affected. The tagger is.

Two caveats, so I am not marking this as more than low:
- The example in the finding wraps at character 17, not 65, so it is made up. A real failure needs a vocabulary term to straddle the 65-character cut.
- Whether Armenian banks wrap mid-word is UNVERIFIED (README and test comments say so). The space join is partly deliberate: the fixture test expects "հաշվից 1570012345670001" as separate tokens. So a plain ""-join would be wrong for banks that wrap at word boundaries.

Still, the code path is reachable and the input is realistic. It fails quietly and gives a misleading reconciliation report. Not refuted, low severity.

The code confirms the mechanism. In Mt940Parser.tokenize, each continuation line is stripped and appended after '\n'. The ':86:' case (line ~90) then replaces '\n' with ' ' and collapses whitespace. CommitService:249 passes that joined description to BankDescriptionTagger.tags(). For long terms such as 'эквайринг' or 'acquiring', the tagger only does a substring match (text.contains). So if a keyword is split across lines, as in 'эквай' + 'ринга', the joined text holds 'эквай ринга' and no 'acquiring' tag is set. ReconciliationService only considers credits with t.tags.contains("acquiring"). That settlement is therefore ignored, and when payment_method is mapped, its sales day can be reported as SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT.

This is not documented or intended anywhere. The README, decision log #11/#12 and the parser Javadoc only say that continuation lines are joined. Decision #11 exists precisely so that tags such as acquiring survive for reconciliation, and this gap undercuts that goal. SWIFT ':86:' is 6×65x, and some banks cut at a fixed width regardless of word boundaries. So the scenario is realistic, but not proven for Armenian banks: the README and the tests both mark the ':86:' wording of Armenian banks as UNVERIFIED, and the synthetic fixture wraps at word boundaries.

The impact is limited, so low severity is right:
- 'POS' often appears in the same description and still matches.
- Without payment_method, only PLAUSIBLE/UNMATCHED lines are affected; no false 'sales without settlement' claim is made.
- PILOT_RUNBOOK tells the operator to 'ask before concluding anything' about SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT.
- It is a reporting error only; no data is lost.

confirmed.title: BankDescriptionTagger: 'վարձ' matches inside 'աշխատավարձ' (salary tagged rent); multi-word terms fail on NBSP or double spaces
confirmed.description: Non-ASCII terms use a plain substring match, and input whitespace is not normalised.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: tags('Աշխատավարձ սեպտեմբեր') = [salary, rent] and tags('Փոխհատուցում վարձատրություն') = [rent]. tags('քարտային  վաճառք') (two spaces) and the NBSP variant give [], so a card settlement described this way is not tagged acquiring and is ignored by reconciliation.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Normalise whitespace (\s+ and NBSP to one space) before matching, and exclude known compounds (check 'աշխատավարձ' before 'վարձ').

verdicts.reasoning:
The code confirms the mechanics. In BankDescriptionTagger.java line 39, `shortAscii = term.length() <= 4 && term.chars().allMatch(c -> c < 128)` is false for every Armenian term, so line 40 runs `return text.contains(term);`, which is a plain substring check. The 'rent' vocabulary is `List.of("վարձ", "аренд", "rent")` (line 20), and "աշխատավարձ" (ա-շ-խ-ա-տ-ա-վ-ա-ր-ձ) ends in "վարձ". So tags("Աշխատավարձ ...") gives {salary, rent}. "վարձատրություն" (remuneration) gives {rent} for the same reason.

Whitespace: the multi-word term "քարտային վաճառք" (line 17) only matches with exactly one ASCII space. tags() only lowercases the text (line 30). RowContext.text() only trims (`v.trim()`, RowContext.java:35). Nothing collapses double spaces, and nothing replaces NBSP for CSV/XLSX input. Mt940Parser.java:90 does `replaceAll("\\s+", " ")`, but Java's `\s` does not match U+00A0. So "քարտային  վաճառք" (two spaces) or the NBSP variant gets no 'acquiring' tag, unless the text also contains another acquiring term ("pos", "էքվայրինգ", ...).

Impact: CommitService.java:249 stores these tags at commit time. The stored description is masked, so the record cannot be re-tagged later (ReconciliationSettings.java:8-9). ReconciliationService.java:96 skips any credit without the 'acquiring' tag (`if (!t.tags.contains("acquiring")) continue;`). A missed tag therefore leaves the settlement unmatched and can raise a false "Card sales with no acquiring credit found in the statement" finding (line 137). That part of the finding holds.

One overstatement: nothing reads the 'rent' and 'salary' tags. The only consumer of description_tags is the 'acquiring' check, so tagging salary as rent is stored but has no visible effect on reports today. Severity stays low: the whitespace miss can cause a misleading reconciliation finding, and the rent mis-tag is a latent issue.

The code does what the finding says, but neither part leads to a wrong result anyone can see.

1) Salary/rent overlap. 'աշխատավարձ' does contain 'վարձ', and non-ASCII terms use a plain `text.contains` (BankDescriptionTagger.java:40), so a salary line also gets the 'rent' tag. However, nothing reads the 'rent', 'salary', 'tax' or 'bank_fee' tags. Tags are written only at CommitService.java:249 into bank_transactions.description_tags. The only reader is ReconciliationService.java:155/162, and its only check is `t.tags.contains("acquiring")` (line 96). No report, KPI, API or AI path uses the 'rent' tag. An extra tag on a salary line therefore changes no output. It is a latent label error with no failure scenario.

2) Double space / NBSP in multi-word terms. The input path is real: the CSV and XLSX parsers only trim cells (XlsxTabularParser:48/65, RowContext.text:35), and only the MT940 parser collapses whitespace (Mt940Parser:90, ASCII \s only). But only two terms contain a space: 'քարտային վաճառք' and 'card settlement'. Every acquiring description in the fixtures and tests contains 'POS' or 'acquiring', which are matched as whole words and are unaffected by spacing. Nothing in the repo shows a real bank export spelling the phrase with a double space or NBSP and without POS or acquiring. The class Javadoc also says the vocabulary is an UNVERIFIED starting point to extend from real statements. If a settlement is missed, the result is SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT, which the runbook (PILOT_RUNBOOK.md:37-38) says to investigate before concluding anything. It is not silent data loss.

So part 1 has no consumer and part 2 depends on hypothetical input formatting. Neither shows a realistic wrong output.

This is a real defect, though a minor one. Low severity is right.

**The code.** In BankDescriptionTagger.java, `containsWord` (lines 38-43) only does a whole-word regex match for ASCII terms of 4 characters or fewer. Every other term goes through plain `text.contains(term)` at line 40. 'աշխատավարձ' (salary) is 'աշխատա' + 'վարձ', so any salary line also contains the rent stem 'վարձ' and gets both tags, [salary, rent]. 'վարձատրություն' (remuneration) gets [rent]. The input is only lowercased, and whitespace is never normalised. So the multi-word term 'քարտային վաճառք' fails to match when the text has a double space or an NBSP. The code comment calls substring matching 'on purpose (inflections)', but that covers suffixes. It does not excuse matching inside a compound word, and nothing in README.md, PILOT_RUNBOOK.md or the decision log documents salary being tagged as rent, or whitespace-sensitive matching.

**Impact.**
- **Rent/salary:** the wrong tag is stored in `bank_transactions.description_tags` (CommitService.java line 249). I found no code that reads the 'rent' or 'salary' tags today; ReconciliationService line 96 only checks 'acquiring'. So right now this is wrong stored data that misleads any later expense categorisation, not a wrong report.
- **Acquiring:** this is the part that matters. ReconciliationSettings and the README both say acquiring credits are recognised *only* by the 'acquiring' tag set at commit, because the stored description is masked. So a settlement described as 'քարտային  վաճառք' (double space or NBSP), with no other trigger word such as 'POS' or 'էքվայրինգ', is never matched. The tag cannot be recomputed later. That day gets a false 'Card sales with no acquiring credit found in the statement' result (SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT).

**Why only low.** The acquiring miss depends on a specific way of writing the description, and many real settlement lines also contain 'POS', which still matches as a whole word. The vocabulary is also marked as a starting point to be extended. Medium would overstate it.

confirmed.title: CSV rows with more fields than the header are silently truncated
confirmed.description: Only header-mapped indexes are read and rec.size() is never compared with the header count, so an unquoted delimiter inside a value shifts the following columns with no warning.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In the bank CSV layout, a description 'Оплата, счет 15' without quotes becomes description='Оплата' and txn_id ('Փաստաթուղթ')=' счет 15'; the real document id is dropped and the row is committed with a wrong id.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Flag or reject records whose field count differs from the header count.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code and the finding holds. In CsvTabularParser.parse (lines 41-47), the only cells read are the ones whose index matches a header name: `for (String h : headers) cells.put(h, rec.isMapped(h) && rec.isSet(h) ? rec.get(h) : "");`. Nothing compares rec.size() with headers.size(). The format at lines 33-38 (DEFAULT with setHeader, skipHeader, trim, ignoreEmptyLines) does not check field counts either. commons-csv 1.14.1 has no strict record-length mode, so a record with extra values parses with no error. Any value past the last header index is dropped, and ParsedRow never carries the raw record, so later code cannot spot the problem.

The scenario matches the real layout. The bank fixture header is `Ամսաթիվ,Մուտք,Ելք,Արժույթ,Մնացորդ,Նշանակում,Փաստաթուղթ`, and in docs/samples/mappings/bank_statement_credit_debit_v1.json description maps to Նշանակում (index 5), txn_id maps to Փաստաթուղթ (index 6), and idColumns is ["Փաստաթուղթ"].

Example row: `01.09.2026,150000,,AMD,2340000,Оплата, счет 15,TRX-88213`. This splits into 8 fields: description becomes 'Оплата', Փաստաթուղթ becomes 'счет 15' (trimmed), and TRX-88213 is silently lost. CommitService line 230 (`String txnId = r.text("txn_id")`) then uses 'счет 15' as the bank reference. The txn_id_derived warning never fires because the value is not blank. The row is inserted with ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, account_ref, txn_id) DO NOTHING. If two such rows share the shifted text, the second one is dropped as a duplicate.

I found no README, decision-log or runbook entry documenting this behavior, and ParsersTest has no test for it. Low severity is fair: it needs a malformed (unquoted) export, but when it happens the wrong id is committed with no warning.

Real usage can reach this. CsvTabularParser.parse (lines 33-48) uses CSVFormat.DEFAULT with a header taken from the first line. Commons CSV 1.14.1 is lenient about records whose length differs from the header: it does not throw, and get(name) simply reads the field at that header's index. The loop at line 44 only goes through the header names and never compares rec.size() with headers.size(), so any fields past the header count are thrown away without a warning.

The real bank layout (test fixture synthetic_bank_statement.csv and docs/samples/mappings/bank_statement_credit_debit_v1.json) is: Ամսաթիվ, Մուտք, Ելք, Արժույթ, Մնացորդ, Նշանակում, Փաստաթուղթ. The description (Նշանակում) is next to last and the document id (Փաստաթուղթ, mapped to txn_id and used as idColumns) is last. If a description contains an unquoted comma, the row gets 8 fields: description becomes the first fragment, txn_id becomes the second fragment (trimmed), and the real document id is lost.

CommitService.java:230 takes r.text("txn_id") as given; it only falls back to a derived hash when the value is null, and it does not check the format. The row is then inserted with ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, account_ref, txn_id) DO NOTHING. So the wrong id gets committed, and two such rows with the same fragment (e.g. 'счет 15') would collide and one would be silently dropped. I found nothing in README, PILOT_RUNBOOK, the decision log or the architecture notes saying that extra fields are allowed.

Mitigating factors: well-formed exporters quote fields that contain a comma, and the first part of the description is kept, so low severity is appropriate. Still, the scenario is reachable through the normal CSV import path with a realistic malformed export.

I confirmed this from the code. CsvTabularParser.parse (lines 41-47) builds each row only from parser.getHeaderNames() and never compares rec.size() with headers.size(). With CSVFormat.DEFAULT plus setHeader(), Commons CSV 1.14 does not object to records that are longer than the header: the extra fields are simply never read. The bank fixture header is `Ամսաթիվ,Մուտք,Ելք,Արժույթ,Մնացորդ,Նշանակում,Փաստաթուղթ`, with description second to last and the document id last. A row like `...,2340000,Оплата, счет 15,TRX-1` therefore has 8 fields. The parser yields description='Оплата' and txn_id='счет 15' (setTrim strips the space), and 'TRX-1' is silently dropped. CommitService.java:230 takes this value as the bank reference, and the derived-id warning is skipped because txn_id is not blank.

The insert at CommitService.java:243-246 uses `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, account_ref, txn_id) DO NOTHING`. So if two shifted rows end up with the same fake txn_id (e.g. both 'счет 15'), the second real transaction is silently discarded.

Nothing in README.md, the decision log (Решения.md) or PILOT_RUNBOOK.md documents ignoring field-count mismatches. The founder doc asks for a data-quality error screen (section 9, Phase 1), and section 11 requires correct handling and no duplicate or wrong records. Silent truncation works against both, so this is not intended behavior.

Low severity is right. It only happens with a malformed CSV (an unquoted delimiter), which real bank exports usually avoid. When the shift moves text into a numeric or date column, the row fails type parsing and is rejected visibly. Silent corruption only happens when the shift lands in trailing text columns, as in the bank layout. I do not raise it to medium: it depends on bad input, though the duplicate-key drop makes it slightly worse than the finding states.

confirmed.title: CSV row numbers drift from the physical file lines after blank lines or multi-line quoted cells
confirmed.description: rowNumber is derived from the CSV record number, but ignored empty lines and embedded newlines are not counted.
confirmed.failure_scenario:
Verified: 'a,b

1,2
"x
y",3
4,5' reports the row '4,5' as row 4 while it is on line 6, so the validation report and CLI 'row N' output point the client at the wrong line.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use parser.getCurrentLineNumber() or the record's character position to report the physical start line.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. CsvTabularParser.java:47 builds the row number as `new ParsedRow((int) rec.getRecordNumber() + 1, cells)`, and the format at lines 33-38 uses `.setIgnoreEmptyLines(true)` with the header taken from the first record. getRecordNumber() counts CSV records, not physical lines. So blank lines that are skipped, and newlines inside quoted cells, are never added to the number.

I ran the finding's input through the project's commons-csv 1.14.1 jar from ~/.m2 with the same format settings (a scratch script using `java`, not a project build). The input was "a,b\n\n1,2\n\"x\ny\",3\n4,5". Output: `2 -> 1,2` (physical line 3), `3 -> x\ny,3` (lines 4-5), `4 -> 4,5` (line 6). When there are no blank lines or multi-line cells the number matches the line (the first data row is 2). Once either appears, the numbers drift.

This number is what the client sees. It goes into ParsedRow.rowNumber, is stored by ImportService.java:84 (`rownum`), is copied into every ValidationIssue by RowContext and CommitService, is written by CommitService.java:82, and is printed by PilotCli.java:84 as `row %d`. The README and the decision notes say nothing about rows being numbered by record rather than by line. A client who opens the CSV in a text editor will look at the wrong line. In a spreadsheet the record count may happen to match, which keeps the severity low.

Severity stays low. Nothing is lost or wrongly accepted; only the location shown in the validation report is wrong.

I could not refute this. The bug is real and normal usage reaches it. CsvTabularParser.java:47 sets rowNumber to rec.getRecordNumber()+1. With setIgnoreEmptyLines(true), commons-csv counts only records, so a skipped blank line or a line break inside a quoted cell does not raise the number.

I ran the exact config against the commons-csv 1.14.1 jar from ~/.m2 using the input 'a,b\n\n1,2\n"x\ny",3\n4,5'. It printed rows 2, 3 and 4, but the records start on file lines 3, 4 and 6.

That number travels the normal import path without being corrected: ParsedRow, then ImportService (stored as rownum in source_records), then RowContext/ValidationIssue, then CommitService (saved as the issue row), then PilotCli:84, which prints "row %d".

confirmed.title: Template text is stored as guard_passed=true without being checked, and fails the guard on negative facts
confirmed.description: TemplateExplanationProvider and Explanation.withFallback hard-code guardPassed=true; the guard never runs on the template at runtime. GuardedExplainer's comment claims the fallback is guard-checked in tests, but TemplateExplanationTest uses one set of positive facts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: For a RESTOCK with on_hand=-5 and days_of_stock=-2.5, guard.check(template text) fails with 'number not in facts: 2.5' (confirmed in a scratch copy), yet the stored row says guard_passed=true. With the LLM on, the LLM's correct '-2.5' is also rejected, so the audit trail claims a verified explanation the guard would reject.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code path and confirmed the finding.

1) The guard never runs on template text, yet the result is stored as guard_passed=true.
- TemplateExplanationProvider.explain ends with `return new Explanation(text, "template", null, PROMPT_VERSION, true, List.of(), null);`. The `true` is hard-coded.
- Explanation.withFallback is `new Explanation(textHy, provider, model, promptVersion, true, rejectedBecause, reason)`, also hard-coded `true`.
- In GuardedExplainer, `guard.check` is called only on the LLM candidate: `GuardResult check = guard.check(candidate.textHy(), r);`. The `llm == null` path (`return template.explain(r);`) and all three fallback paths never call the guard on the template.
- RecommendationService then saves `.param("gp", e.guardPassed())` into guard_passed.
- The class comment says "The template output is itself guard-checked in tests". The decision log (#15) says "каждый ответ проверяет guard" (every answer is checked by the guard). Neither is true at runtime.

2) Negative facts are reachable.
- CommitService.inventory accepts any quantity (`r.decimal("quantity", true)`). It has no sign check, and the migration has no CHECK constraint.
- KpiService computes `daysOfStock = stock.divide(velocity, 1, HALF_UP)` whenever velocity > 0. So stock -5 at velocity 2 gives days_of_stock = -2.5.
- RecommendationEngine fires RESTOCK whenever `x.daysOfStock().compareTo(restockBelowDays) < 0`, and -2.5 is below the threshold. It stores the facts on_hand=-5, daily_velocity=2.000 and days_of_stock=-2.5.

3) The guard rejects the template text for these facts.
- The template writes `dec(f.get("days_of_stock"))`, which is "-2.5".
- The guard's NUMBER regex `\d{1,3}(?:[  ,.]\d{3})+(?:[.,]\d+)?|\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?` has no sign, so it extracts the token "2.5". `interpretations()` turns that into {25, 2.5}.
- `allowedNumbers` contains -2.5, -3 (HALF_UP scale 0 of -2.5) and the small counts 0..10. Neither 25 nor 2.5 is in that set, so the guard reports "number not in facts: 2.5" and passes=false.
- The "5" from on_hand=-5 slips through only because 5 is in the 0..10 small-count list.

4) With the LLM on, an LLM text that correctly says "-2.5" is rejected the same way. The code falls back to the template with fallback_reason=guard_rejected and still guard_passed=true. That stored text would fail the same check.

Impact: the audit trail claims the stored text passed the guard when the guard would have rejected it. This is misleading provenance, but the client sees no wrong numbers, so low severity is right.

Sale rows are different: line 119 warns on a negative quantity, but inventory rows get no such check. The `inventory_snapshots.quantity` column (V2 migration) is `numeric(18,3) NOT NULL` with no CHECK constraint. POS exports with negative on-hand stock are common.

2. **Negative stock produces a RESTOCK.** `KpiService` (around lines 147-153) computes `daysOfStock = stock / velocity`. With negative stock and positive velocity this comes out negative. `RecommendationEngine` (lines 37-43) then emits RESTOCK, because the value is below `restockBelowDays` and velocity is above 0. The facts become on_hand=-5, daily_velocity=2, days_of_stock=-2.5.

3. **The template text would fail the guard, but it is never checked.** `TemplateExplanationProvider.dec()` writes "-2.5" using `toPlainString`. The guard's `NUMBER` regex ignores the minus sign, so it extracts "2.5". The allowed set is {-5, 2, -2.5, -3, 0..10}, and 2.5 is not in it, so the guard reports "number not in facts: 2.5". "5" only passes because small counts 0..10 are always allowed.
   - Even so, `TemplateExplanationProvider` hard-codes `guardPassed=true` and `Explanation.withFallback` forces `true`. `GuardedExplainer` never calls `guard.check` on template output.
   - `RecommendationService` (line 76) stores `e.guardPassed()` in `recommendations.guard_passed`.

4. **The behavior contradicts the decision log and the code comment.** Decision #15 says "каждый ответ проверяет guard" (every response is checked by the guard). The `GuardedExplainer` Javadoc claims the template is guard-checked in tests, but the tests only use positive AD_TEST and RESTOCK facts.

5. **With the LLM on, a correct answer is thrown away.** If the LLM correctly writes "-2.5", the guard rejects it and the template is used instead. The row is stored with `fallback_reason=guard_rejected`, `guard_passed=true`, and a false rejection reason. That adds noise to the manual review of `guard_rejected` rows that the eval doc asks for.

**Why the severity is low:** the template text itself states the facts correctly. The actual faults are the sign-blind guard and an audit flag that records an unchecked result as passed. Nothing wrong is shown to the client and no data is lost. The impact is limited to provenance, rejected correct LLM answers, and misleading review entries. I found no negative-stock rows in `retail_test` (0 rows in total).

**What the code does**
- `TemplateExplanationProvider.explain` always returns `guardPassed=true`.
- `Explanation.withFallback` (line 10) also hard-codes `true`.
- `GuardedExplainer` never calls `guard.check` on template text, whether the LLM is off or the template is used as a fallback.
- The `Explanation` javadoc says `guardPassed` means "whether the guard accepted it". V4 stores this value in `recommendations.guard_passed NOT NULL`.

**Docs**
- Decision log item 15 (vault/00-Index/Решения.md) says "каждый ответ проверяет guard" (the guard checks every answer).
- README lines 97-99 describe the guard as a gate with the template as the fallback.
- The `GuardedExplainer` javadoc says the template is guard-checked only in tests. `TemplateExplanationTest` uses fixed positive facts.

**The negative-fact case is reachable**
- `CommitService.inventory` accepts any quantity. There is no sign check, and the column is `numeric(18,3) NOT NULL` with no CHECK.
- `KpiService` adds up snapshot quantities per SKU across warehouses and computes `daysOfStock = stock / velocity` whenever `velocity > 0`. Negative stock therefore gives negative `days_of_stock`.

- The template writes "-2.5" for `days_of_stock`.
- `ExplanationGuard.NUMBER` has no sign handling, so it reads only the token "2.5".

- "3500" becomes " 00", which also parses to 0.
- allowedNumbers() always allows 0..10 (line 72: `for (int i = 0; i <= 10; i++) out.add(BigDecimal.valueOf(i));`), so neither number is reported. A made-up revenue figure passes the guard.

The skuCode comes from RecommendationEngine (line 115, x.skuCode()), and ClaudeExplanationProvider sends it to the LLM as "sku_code" (line 82), so the LLM sees it and can echo or invent numbers around it. GuardedExplainer is the only path to the client, and decision #15 says every LLM answer is checked by the guard. Short numeric item codes are realistic in accounting exports, so the guard's purpose ("a false acceptance costs the client's trust") is defeated in a reachable case. The same partial-substring problem can also turn a disallowed number into an allowed small one, for example a code "2" turns "25" into " 5", which reads as 5.

The second scenario, a product name containing "50%", is weaker. Line 57 only removes the exact full name string. A standalone "50%" outside the name is still matched and rejected unless 50 is a fact, so that part is mostly reproducing the name word for word, which is arguably intended.

**The code does what the finding says.** In ExplanationGuard.java, line 56 runs `s = s.replace(r.skuCode(), " ")` on the whole text before the NUMBER regex runs (lines 41-49). The replace matches the code anywhere, not only as a whole word.

**Nothing stops a numeric SKU code.**
- RecommendationEngine:115 builds the Recommendation from `x.skuCode()` and `x.name()`. These come from KpiService, which reads `sale_lines.sku_code` and `products.name`.
- CommitService:99 takes the code with `r.required("sku_code")` and does not check its format.
- The V2 migration declares `sku_code` as plain `text NOT NULL`, with no CHECK.
- A client file can therefore contain a code like "35", "1001" or "00012".

**The guard sees real LLM output.** GuardedExplainer is the only way explanations reach the client (decision 15 in the decision log). It checks the text that ClaudeExplanationProvider returns. That provider sends `sku_code` and `sku_name` to the model, so the model can echo them.

**What goes wrong.** Take sku_code "35" and the text "35000 ... 3500". After stripping, "35000" becomes " 000" and "3500" becomes " 00". Both read as 0, which is in the allowed 0..10 set, so made-up figures pass the guard. In general, any made-up number that contains the code's digits is broken into pieces, and those pieces are checked instead of the real value. The class comment says a false acceptance costs the client's trust, so this weakens a stated safety net.

**Limits on the finding.**
- The bundled sample file uses codes like "A-1045", which do not trigger this. Only purely numeric or very short codes do.
- It only matters when the LLM has already invented a number, and that number has to contain the code's digits.
- The product-name half (numbers repeated from the name go unchecked) is weaker. Names come from the client's own data, and repeating them is partly intended.

Low severity is about right.

I confirmed this from the code. In ExplanationGuard.java:56-57, stripAllowedLiterals calls a plain String.replace(r.skuCode(), " ") on the whole text before the NUMBER regex runs. Nothing limits the match to whole tokens. With sku_code "35", the text "35000" becomes " 000" and "3500" becomes " 00". Both then parse to 0, and 0 is always allowed because allowedNumbers adds 0..10. A code like "1" is worse: it strips that digit from every number, so "11000" becomes "  000" and also passes.

No documentation makes this intended. README:98 and decision #15 in Решения.md say every number must come from the facts. The class Javadoc says the guard is "deliberately strict: a false acceptance costs the client's trust". The eval coverage note lists case 18 (prompt injection) as covered by "guard на выходе" (the output guard). Silently accepting invented numbers breaks the founder's AI rule that numbers come only from engine facts.

Purely numeric SKU codes are realistic in POS/accounting exports. The column is free text (products.sku_code), and only tests use alphanumeric codes like "A-1".

confirmed.title: Return classification is asserted only as 'returns > 0' although the fixture has exactly 11 returns
confirmed.description: The HC fixture has 11 'Վերադարձ գնորդից' rows out of 313. The test asserts returns > 0 and sales + returns == committed; the second holds for any split because there are only two operation types, and maxQty <= 3 checks nothing about returns.
confirmed.failure_scenario: isReturn is changed to contains("Վ"). All 313 rows, including 'Վաճառք (Մանրածախ)' sales, are stored as RETURN and CommitServiceIT passes.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Assert returns == 11 and sales == 302.

verdicts.reasoning:
I confirmed this from the code and the fixture. The assertion is weak as described, and severity stays low.

Fixture: I read src/test/resources/fixtures/synthetic_hc_sales.xlsx with openpyxl. It has 313 data rows: 'Վաճառք (Մանրածախ)' 154, 'Վաճառք (Կտրոն)' 148 and 'Վերադարձ գնորդից' 11. So the expected split is exactly 11 returns and 302 sales.

Test, CommitServiceIT.java lines 76-83:
- `assertThat(returns).isGreaterThan(0);`
- `assertThat(sales + returns).isEqualTo(first.rowsCommitted());`
- `assertThat(products).isEqualTo(5);`
- `assertThat(maxQty).isLessThanOrEqualTo(new BigDecimal("3"));`

Production code, CommitService.java:115 sets `operation = isReturn(opRaw, s) ? "RETURN" : "SALE"`. Line 264-267 compares exactly: `markers.stream().anyMatch(m -> opRaw.trim().equalsIgnoreCase(m.trim()))`. The current code is correct; the gap is only in the test.

Mutation scenario: if `isReturn` became `opRaw.contains("Վ")`, every row would become RETURN, because 'Վաճառք' also starts with Վ. The four assertions would still pass:
- returns = 313 > 0
- sales + returns = 0 + 313 = rowsCommitted
- there are still 5 products
- the maximum quantity is unchanged

A partial misclassification, such as tagging 'Վաճառք (Կտրոն)' rows as RETURN, would also pass this test.

Mitigation, which supports the low severity: WeeklyReportServiceIT commits the same fixture and asserts `net > 0` on the summary sheet. That would likely catch the all-RETURN mutation at suite level, though not necessarily a partial one. The finding's specific claim is true: CommitServiceIT alone passes under that mutation. `assertThat(returns).isEqualTo(11)` and `assertThat(sales).isEqualTo(302)` would close the gap.

I'm rejecting this finding. It describes a weak test, not a production defect. CommitService.isReturn (CommitService.java:264) does an exact, case-insensitive match against the configured returnMarkers, and nothing in production code can reach the bug the finding imagines. The failure scenario is a made-up future change to the code (isReturn becoming contains("Վ")), not an input or state that real usage can produce.

Even that imagined regression would not get past the test suite. WeeklyReportServiceIT imports the same synthetic_hc_sales.xlsx file with the same return marker, commits it, and asserts that net sales for September 2026 is greater than 0. If every row were stored as RETURN, KpiService would subtract every row from netSales (KpiService.java:118-124), net sales would be negative, and that assertion would fail. The opposite mistake, where returns are never recognised, is caught by CommitServiceIT's own returns > 0 check. KpiServiceIT also checks the exact return amount for a RETURN line (29166.67).

Asserting exactly 11 returns and 302 sales would be a tighter test. But the task excludes "consider adding" suggestions, and this finding is one: no realistic input leads to wrong output, data loss or a misleading report.

I could not refute this. The weak assertion is real, but the suite as a whole catches the exact scenario the finding gives, so low severity is right.

**What the test checks.** `CommitServiceIT.java` lines 76-82 check three things:
- `returns > 0`
- `sales + returns == rowsCommitted`
- `max(quantity) <= 3`

The method name is `hcSales_areCommittedTyped_returnsRecognized_andRecommitIsNoop`.

**What the fixture contains.** I read `src/test/resources/fixtures/synthetic_hc_sales.xlsx` with openpyxl. It has 313 rows:
- 'Վաճառք (Մանրածախ)': 154
- 'Վաճառք (Կտրոն)': 148
- 'Վերադարձ գնորդից': 11

So the exact answer, 11 returns and 302 sales, is known and never asserted.

**Why the other two checks don't help.** `CommitService` (around line 115) only ever writes 'RETURN' or 'SALE'. That makes the sum check true for any split. The quantity bound says nothing about how rows were classified.

**Why it is not intended behavior.** Nothing in README.md or the decision log says this loose check is on purpose. The founder's acceptance criteria (section 11, line 146) require returns to be handled correctly.

**Why the mutation is already caught.** If `isReturn` became `contains("Վ")`, every row would be stored as RETURN and CommitServiceIT would pass, as the finding says. But `WeeklyReportServiceIT` commits the same fixture and asserts net sales > 0. In `KpiService`, RETURN rows only subtract from net sales, so with every row a RETURN net sales goes negative and that test fails. Two other mistakes also get caught:
- Labelling the 148 'Կտրոն' sales as returns gives 159 returns against 154 sales, which very likely also pushes net sales negative.
- Missing every return gives `returns == 0`, which fails `returns > 0`.

**What still slips through.** A regression that misses only some returns. For example, a trim or marker-variant issue that affects a few of the 11 rows. CommitServiceIT would still pass and the error would be small enough not to flip net sales. This is a missing test check, not a production bug, so the low severity stands.

confirmed.title: Card detection by substring counts gift cards, bonus cards and split-tender payments as card sales
confirmed.description: isCard() is p.contains(marker) with the markers card, քարտ, карта and pos. Gift cards ('Նվեր քարտ', 'Gift card'), bonus cards ('Бонусная карта') and split tenders such as 'Կանխիկ/Քարտ' all count as acquiring-settled card sales at the full line amount. 'pos' also matches inside words such as 'deposit'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A day has bank-card sales of 480,000 plus 20,000 paid by gift certificate ('Նվեր քարտ'), and the settlement is 470,400 (a 2% fee on 480,000). The code compares it with 500,000, giving a rate of 5.92% > 3%, so the credit is UNMATCHED and the day becomes SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT. With a smaller gift amount, the credit is MATCHED with an inflated implied fee.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use an explicit per-client mapping of payment_method values to CARD, CASH or OTHER. Treat unknown values as unknown rather than matching substrings, and split mixed tenders.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the code path and the defect is real.

1. **Raw value is stored.** CommitService.java:136 stores the raw text with `.param("pm", r.text("payment_method"))`. V3__reconciliation.sql:15 confirms this: `payment_method text; -- raw value, classified at reconcile time`. Nothing normalizes the value at import.

2. **Substring matching against default markers.** ReconciliationSettings.defaults() uses `List.of("card", "քարտ", "карта", "pos")`. WeeklyReportService.java:72 always calls the service with `ReconciliationSettings.defaults()`. ReconciliationService.java:219-222 does the check:
   ```java
   String p = paymentMethod.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
   return markers.stream().anyMatch(m -> p.contains(m.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)));
   ```
   So these values all count as card:
   - 'Նվեր քարտ' (contains 'քարտ')
   - 'Gift card' (contains 'card')
   - 'Бонусная карта' (contains 'карта')
   - 'Կանխիկ/Քարտ' (contains 'քարտ' after lowercasing)
   - 'Deposit' (contains 'pos')

   This is unlike BankDescriptionTagger.java:37, which requires short ASCII terms such as "pos" to be whole words. No such guard exists here.

3. **Gift-card amount lands in card sales.** In dailySales, lines 179-180 run `if (cardOnly && !isCard(pm, cardMarkers)) return; ... out.merge(d, paid, add)`. The gift-card group's amount is therefore added to that day's card sales.

4. **The settlement fails the fee check.** Lines 103-106 compute `diff = sales - t.amount; rate = diff/sales`, and the line is MATCHED only if `0 <= rate <= maxFeeRate (0.03)`. With sales of 500,000 and a settlement of 470,400, rate = 29,600 / 500,000 = 0.0592 > 0.03, so it is not matched at that lag. Unless another lag day happens to fit, `best == null`, the credit is UNMATCHED (line 116), and the day is never added to claimedDays.

5. **The day is reported as missing its settlement.** Step 3 (lines 129-134) then emits `SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT` for that day. The report wrongly says the card sales had no acquiring credit.

6. **Smaller gift amounts inflate the fee.** If the gift amount is small enough that the rate stays at or below 3%, the credit is MATCHED with an inflated implied fee, which skews `avgFee`.

**Not documented as intended.** The README and runbook only say to add `payment_method` to the mapping. Neither mentions gift, bonus or split tenders, nor the substring caveat.

**Severity.** Low is appropriate. The failure depends on the client's POS producing such tender labels, and it only distorts reconciliation status and fee figures. It does not lose or corrupt data.

Real usage can reach this code. CommitService.java:136 stores the raw mapped `payment_method` text with no normalisation, and V3 says it is "classified at reconcile time". PILOT_RUNBOOK.md (the «Համադրում» section) tells the operator to add `payment_method` to the HC mapping, and README's "Next" item does the same. Classification is done only by isCard() (ReconciliationService.java:219-223), a case-insensitive `contains` check against ReconciliationSettings.defaults() = ["card","քարտ","карта","pos"]. The only production caller is WeeklyReportService.java:72, which always passes `ReconciliationSettings.defaults()`. So the Settings javadoc says the markers are "assumptions to confirm per client", but the code gives no way to override them per client. Any tender label containing one of those substrings counts as a card sale at the full line amount. Common Armenian and Russian retail labels do: "Նվեր քարտ" (gift card), "Բոնուս քարտ", "Бонусная карта", or a mixed "Կանխիկ/Քարտ". Their day totals go into salesByDay (dailySales, lines 177-181).

The fee-rate check (lines 104-110) then compares the settlement with the inflated total. The finding's numbers check out. With 480,000 card sales, 20,000 gift-card sales and a settlement of 470,400, the rate is (500,000 − 470,400) / 500,000 = 5.92%, above the 3% maximum. The credit becomes UNMATCHED and the day is reported as SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT. With smaller non-card amounts the credit is still MATCHED, but the "Implied acquiring fee" is inflated.

No DB constraint, mapping setting or parser step filters these values. Tests use only "Card", "Cash", "Քարտ" and "card", so they never check this. Severity stays low for three reasons. The runbook tells the operator to "ask before concluding anything" on SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT. The exact HC export labels are not yet verified. And it is a misleading report, not data loss. The "pos"-inside-"deposit" part is weaker and speculative, but the gift-card and split-tender cases are realistic and confirmed from the code.

I confirmed this from the code. It is not documented as intended behaviour.

**What the code does**
- `ReconciliationService.java:219-222`: `isCard` lowercases `payment_method` and returns true if any marker is a substring of it.
- `ReconciliationSettings.defaults()` sets the markers to `card`, `քարտ`, `карта` and `pos`.
- `dailySales` (lines 167-182) adds up the full paid amount of every `sale_lines` group whose `payment_method` matches any of these.
- So all of these count as card sales that the acquiring bank should settle:
  - 'Նվեր քարտ' or 'Gift card' (gift cards)
  - 'Бонусная карта' (bonus card)
  - 'Կանխիկ/Քարտ' (cash and card on one value)
  - any value that contains 'pos' (deposit, posted and so on)
- In practice the markers cannot be changed per client. The only caller, `WeeklyReportService.java:72`, always passes `ReconciliationSettings.defaults()`.
- `BankDescriptionTagger` already guards against this kind of error: its comment says short ASCII terms like "pos" must match as whole words. `isCard` has no such guard, so the risk was known on the bank side but not handled on the sales side.

**What the docs say**
- The README says thresholds are "assumptions in `ReconciliationSettings`", and the settings Javadoc says the defaults should be confirmed per client and bank.
- Neither the README, the decision log (entries 11 and 12 only cover masking and the PLAUSIBLE-without-payment-method rule) nor the runbook says that gift cards, bonus cards or mixed tenders should count as acquiring card sales.
- Counting non-acquiring tenders inflates the card-sales figure. That leads to false UNMATCHED and SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT results, or to MATCHED results with an inflated implied fee.
- The scenario in the finding checks out against the code. (480,000 + 20,000 = 500,000 compared with 470,400 gives a rate of 5.92%, above the 3% limit, so the credit is UNMATCHED and the day is reported as SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT.)

**Why the severity stays low**
- The README's "Next" section says `payment_method` is not yet in the real HC mapping. Until it is, the code uses the TOTAL_SALES_PROXY/PLAUSIBLE path, and `isCard` is never called.
- The runbook tells the operator to "ask before concluding anything" about SALES_WITHOUT_SETTLEMENT.
- The bug does not touch the founder's acceptance criteria on internal transfers or tenant isolation.
- So it is a real but contained defect that can make the reconciliation sheet misleading.

confirmed.title: Days of stock is rounded to 1 decimal before the RESTOCK and slow-mover threshold comparisons
confirmed.description: daysOfStock = stock.divide(velocity, 1, HALF_UP) is compared with the thresholds after rounding. KpiService:154 compares it with > slowMoverDays, and RecommendationEngine:38 compares it with < restockBelowDays. Values just across a threshold are rounded back onto it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified in jshell. 750 units sold in 30 days gives a velocity of 25. With a stock of 349 the true value is 13.96 days, which rounds to 14.0, so '< 14' is false and no RESTOCK is issued. 900 units in 30 days with a stock of 2,701 gives 90.03 days, which rounds to 90.0, so '> 90' is false and the SKU is not a slow mover.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare the unrounded quotient, or compare stock with threshold x velocity, and round only for display.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. The code path does what the finding says. In KpiService.java:146, `velocity = netUnits.divide(periodDays, CALC_SCALE=10, HALF_UP)`. Line 153 then computes `daysOfStock = stock.divide(velocity, 1, RoundingMode.HALF_UP)`, so the value is rounded to one decimal place. Line 154 compares that rounded value: `slow = stock.signum() > 0 && daysOfStock.compareTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(settings.slowMoverDays())) > 0`. The same rounded value goes into SkuKpi at line 161. RecommendationEngine.java:38 also compares it: `x.daysOfStock().compareTo(BigDecimal.valueOf(s.restockBelowDays())) < 0`. RecommendationSettings sets restockBelowDays to 14 by default.

Checking the stated inputs, with a 30-day period (from..to inclusive gives periodDays = 30):
- 750 net units gives a velocity of exactly 25. With a stock of 349, 349/25 = 13.96, which becomes 14.0 at scale 1 with HALF_UP. `14.0.compareTo(14) == 0`, so `< 0` is false and no RESTOCK is issued, although the true cover is below 14 days.
- 900 units gives a velocity of 30. With a stock of 2,701, 2701/30 = 90.033…, which becomes 90.0. `compareTo(90) == 0`, so `> 0` is false and the SKU is not flagged as a slow mover, although the true value is above 90.

README.md:54 documents days of stock and the "slowMover > 90 days" rule. It does not mention that the threshold is applied to a value already rounded to one decimal place, so this is not documented intended behavior. The effect is limited to a band of about ±0.05 days around each threshold, so severity stays low.

The finding holds. The code matches it, and ordinary data reaches it.

**Where it happens**
- `KpiService.java:153` computes `daysOfStock = stock.divide(velocity, 1, HALF_UP)`. The velocity has `CALC_SCALE = 10`, but this quotient keeps only one decimal.
- `KpiService.java:154` uses that rounded value for the slow-mover test: `daysOfStock > slowMoverDays`.
- `RecommendationEngine.java:38` uses the same rounded `SkuKpi.daysOfStock()` for the restock test: `< restockBelowDays`. No unrounded value is kept anywhere.

**How real usage reaches it**
- Stock comes from inventory snapshots and velocity from net units ÷ period days. Both are ordinary data, so any true value in [restockBelowDays − 0.05, restockBelowDays) rounds up to the threshold.
- With velocity 25/day and 349 on hand, the true value is 13.96 and the stored value is 14.0. `14.0 < 14` is false, so no RESTOCK is issued.
- In the same way, 90.00–90.049 rounds to 90.0 and is not flagged as a slow mover.

**Nothing documents it as intended**
- README:54 says only "slowMover > 90 days". `SkuKpi.java:18` says "daysOfStock > 90". `vault/40-Архитектура/KPI и формулы.md` defines the formula without any rounding step.
- So the rounding before comparison is not a documented decision.

**Why the severity stays low**
- The affected band is 0.05 days wide.
- The value the user sees (14.0) agrees with the decision taken, so the report is not internally contradictory.
- The effect is a missed or late RESTOCK or SLOW_MOVER on borderline SKUs, not data loss or wrong money figures.

It is reachable and real, but minor.

The code matches the finding. At KpiService.java:153 the value is computed as `daysOfStock = stock.divide(velocity, 1, RoundingMode.HALF_UP)`. Line 154 compares that rounded value with `> slowMoverDays`, and RecommendationEngine.java:38 compares the same rounded `x.daysOfStock()` with `< restockBelowDays`. Both thresholds are integers, so a true value inside 0.05 days of a threshold rounds onto it and fails the strict comparison. Example: 13.96 rounds to 14.0, `< 14` is false, and no RESTOCK is issued. The same happens with 90.03, which rounds to 90.0.

None of the design notes say the threshold should be applied to the rounded value. README:54 defines days of stock as stock ÷ net units per day and slowMover as > 90 days. The decision log, the architecture notes (KPI и формулы.md) and the founder document have nothing on this rounding. So this is not intended behaviour. It is a small inconsistency against the documented formula.

Severity should stay low. The error is at most 0.05 days on thresholds that are rough heuristics already: a 14-day restock line and a 90-day slow-mover line. The missed or extra signal is also consistent with the 14.0 or 90.0 the report shows, so a user is not misled in any meaningful way. Nothing is lost or isolated wrongly. This is a real edge-case defect in the rules, not a refutable non-issue, but its impact is minimal.

confirmed.title: Recommendations are sorted by ascending days of stock for all types, so the mildest slow movers fill the slots and dead stock is dropped
confirmed.description: The secondary sort key is days_of_stock ascending, with a missing value treated as Long.MAX. That order is correct for RESTOCK (most urgent first) but backwards for SLOW_MOVER, where more days, or zero velocity, is worse. With maxRecommendations = 3, and ASK_ACCOUNTANT replacing the last slot, the worst slow movers are cut first.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The run has AD_TEST plus three slow movers: X (95 days), Y (4,000 days, 2,000 units at cost) and Z (1 sold, 1 returned, zero velocity, 500 units on hand). The output is AD_TEST, X(95), Y, and if VAT or COGS is unknown, ASK_ACCOUNTANT replaces Y. The owner sees the 95-day item, and the stock tying up the most money (Y, Z) is never shown.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Sort SLOW_MOVER by stock value at cost, or by days of stock descending with zero velocity first. Keep ascending order only for RESTOCK.

verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed from the code. In RecommendationEngine.java lines 82-83, every recommendation is sorted by priority and then by days_of_stock ascending, whatever its type:
`all.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(Recommendation::priority).thenComparing(r -> r.facts().getOrDefault("days_of_stock", BigDecimal.valueOf(Long.MAX_VALUE))));`

SLOW_MOVER entries all have priority 3 (line 56), so among themselves they are ordered only by that key. Ascending order is right for RESTOCK, where fewer days is more urgent, but backwards for SLOW_MOVER.

In KpiService.java lines 150-157, an item with stock but zero net velocity keeps daysOfStock = null and gets `slow = stock.signum() > 0`. RecommendationEngine line 51 then leaves out the days_of_stock fact, so such an item sorts as Long.MAX_VALUE: it is always the last slow mover and the first one cut.

The cut happens at line 84: `all.subList(0, Math.min(all.size(), s.maxRecommendations()))`, and the default maxRecommendations is 3 (RecommendationSettings line 6). When VAT or COGS is unknown, line 87 then overwrites the last slot with ASK_ACCOUNTANT.

The finding's scenario traces exactly. AD_TEST (priority 2) comes first, then X (95 days), then Y (4,000 days), and Z (zero velocity) is dropped. With a critical ask, Y is replaced as well. The owner sees the mildest slow mover while the dead stock is never shown.

Nothing in the documentation makes this ordering intended. README line 95 only says "max 3, accountant question kept", and the decision log and architecture notes say nothing about slow-mover ordering. The founder's spec (section 1, line 17; Inventory Analyst, line 114) asks the system to surface what to review. This is a real but low-impact prioritisation defect: the report is misleading, there is no data loss, and the slow-mover rows still appear on the SKU sheet of the weekly report.

The finding holds: real usage reaches this path, and it produces the misleading order described.

1. RecommendationEngine.java:82-83 sorts all recommendations by priority, then by `days_of_stock` ascending. A missing value counts as Long.MAX_VALUE, so it sorts last. The same order applies to every type, and SLOW_MOVER is not handled separately.

2. Production uses this code. RecommendationService.java:51 calls `engine.recommend(..., RecommendationSettings.defaults())`, and `defaults()` sets maxRecommendations to 3 (RecommendationSettings.java:6). The README (line 95) documents only the cap of 3 and that the accountant question is kept. It says nothing about how slow movers are ranked, so this order is not documented intended behavior.

3. KpiService.java:148-156 produces the inputs the scenario needs:
   - Positive velocity: `daysOfStock = stock / velocity`, and the SKU is a slow mover when that exceeds 90, so X at 95 days and Y at 4,000 days are both possible.
   - Zero or negative net velocity (for example 1 sold and 1 returned) with stock above zero: the SKU is a slow mover with `daysOfStock = null`. The engine then leaves `days_of_stock` out of the facts (line 51), so it sorts last as Long.MAX.

4. All slow movers share priority 3, so the secondary key alone decides which ones fill the remaining slots. The mildest one (just over 90 days) ranks first. The worst ones (very large or unknown days of stock, which means zero sales) are cut first.

5. With AD_TEST (priority 2) plus three slow movers, the output is AD_TEST, X(95), Y, and Z is dropped. If VAT_UNKNOWN or COGS_MISSING is set, lines 85-87 replace the last slot with ASK_ACCOUNTANT, leaving only AD_TEST and X. That is exactly the failure scenario in the finding.

6. Nothing upstream prevents this: there is no constraint and no setting that changes the order. The eval case 12 in the vault ("zero sales plus stock → slow mover") is exactly the zero-velocity case that this sort pushes to the bottom.

The impact is a misleading report: the worst dead stock is hidden while a borderline item is shown. Nothing crashes and no data is lost, so severity low or medium is appropriate.

Confirmed in the code. In RecommendationEngine.java, lines 82-83 sort every recommendation by priority, then by days_of_stock ascending. A missing value counts as Long.MAX_VALUE. SLOW_MOVER is priority 3 and is built at lines 47-57; its days_of_stock fact is added only when it is non-null. KpiService (lines 150-156) sets daysOfStock to null when velocity is 0 or less and still marks the SKU slow when it has stock. So among slow movers, the mildest ones (smallest days over the 90-day threshold) come first, and items with zero sales and stock on hand always come last. Line 84 then cuts the list to maxRecommendations (3 by default in RecommendationSettings). When VAT or COGS is unknown, line 87 also replaces the last slot with ASK_ACCOUNTANT. Together these cut the worst slow movers first.

Nothing documents this order as intended. README line 95 only says "max 3, accountant question kept when VAT/COGS are unknown", and the decision log, runbook and architecture notes say nothing about how slow movers are ranked. It also works against the founder's intent. Eval case 12 ("20 days without sales + stock → slow mover") and the founder doc's Inventory Analyst role describe exactly the zero-velocity dead-stock case, and that case sorts last and is the most likely to be dropped. No test covers ordering among several slow movers.

Severity low is right. Only the ranking among priority-3 items is affected. Higher-priority items (RESTOCK, AD_TEST) usually fill the slots anyway. The system makes no wrong numbers and does no data harm. The owner sees a less important slow-mover recommendation and misses the one tying up the most money.

confirmed.title: --vat-rate is not validated: '20' (percent) is accepted and divides net sales by 21
confirmed.description: vatRate is parsed with new BigDecimal(...) and used as the divisor 1 + rate, with no range check (for example 0 <= rate < 1). The report never prints the rate it used, so a percent-style input does not show in the output.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The operator runs --vat-rate=20, meaning 20%. Verified: 70,000 incl. VAT becomes net 3,333.33. Net sales fall 21x, GP goes deeply negative and AD_TEST disappears, and the summary shows no flag or error.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reject rates outside [0, 1), or interpret values >= 1 as percent with a warning. Print the VAT rate used in the formula notes.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding holds as described. The code path matches it line by line.

1. **No validation on input.** In `ReportCommand.java:38` the value is used as typed: `new BigDecimal(opt(args, "vat-rate", d.vatRate().toPlainString()))`. There is no range check there, and the `KpiSettings` record (`kpi/KpiSettings.java:9-17`) has no validating constructor.

2. **The rate is used directly as a divisor.** In `KpiService.java:91` the code does `BigDecimal vatDivisor = BigDecimal.ONE.add(settings.vatRate());`. Then for every group where `vat_included = true`, it runs `netGroup = netGroup.divide(vatDivisor, CALC_SCALE, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);`. With `--vat-rate=20` the divisor is 21, so 70,000 becomes 3,333.33.

3. **Returns are hit too.** Returns go through the same division, so they are also understated. Net sales, gross profit and contribution are all wrong.

4. **The wrong rate is invisible in the report.**
   - `WeeklyReportService.summarySheet` (lines 111-146) prints only the formula version, currency and text notes such as "առանց ԱԱՀ, եթե ԱԱՀ-ի հիմքը հայտնի է". It never prints `settings.vatRate()`.
   - No flag checks the rate. The only VAT flag is `VAT_UNKNOWN`, which is raised only when `vat_included` is null.
   - The output carries the `FORMULAS_NOT_CONFIRMED` flag by default, but that flag says nothing about the rate value.

5. **Mitigating point.** The README (line 68) and the class Javadoc document the format as a fraction (`--vat-rate=0.20`). So `20` is a misuse of a documented format, which keeps the severity low.

6. **A worse input than the one in the finding.** `--vat-rate=-1` makes the divisor zero. `divide` then throws `ArithmeticException` and the report crashes. Other values silently produce a nonsense report with no indication of the rate used.

The described failure (21x lower net sales, negative gross profit, no flag) occurs as stated. Severity: low.

Real usage can reach this. The `--vat-rate` option is a documented argument of the `--report.run` pilot CLI (README lines 64-69, Javadoc at ReportCommand.java:18). ReportCommand.java:38 passes the raw string into `new BigDecimal(...)`. KpiSettings is a plain record with no compact-constructor validation. KpiService.java:91 computes `vatDivisor = BigDecimal.ONE.add(settings.vatRate())` and divides every `vat_included = true` group by it. Nothing checks the range anywhere, so `--vat-rate=20` gives a divisor of 21, and net sales and GP collapse without any flag. The report output does not show the rate that was used: the formula note at WeeklyReportService.java:122 only says "without VAT if the VAT basis is known", and no line prints the rate. A wrong rate is therefore invisible to the reader of the summary.

What limits severity: the documentation consistently shows the fraction form (0.20), and the default is 0.20, so the failure needs an operator to type the wrong format in an internal pilot CLI. That is a realistic operator mistake, not an impossible state, so the finding stands.

A related unmentioned case: `--vat-rate=-1` makes the divisor zero, which would throw an ArithmeticException.

Severity low is appropriate.

The finding holds. In ReportCommand.java:38 the rate is parsed with `new BigDecimal(opt(args, "vat-rate", ...))`, and the KpiSettings record (kpi/KpiSettings.java) has no compact constructor or range check. KpiService.java:91 then computes `vatDivisor = BigDecimal.ONE.add(settings.vatRate())` and applies it to every VAT-included line. So `--vat-rate=20` gives a divisor of 21, and net sales come out about 1/21 of what they should be. Nothing reports this: the summary sheet in WeeklyReportService.java:115 shows only the period, the formula version and the currency, never the VAT rate used, and no flag covers the case. The result is a report that misleads without any warning: net sales and GP are wrong, and the advice built from them changes.

This is not intended or documented behavior. The README (line 68) and the javadoc only show `--vat-rate=0.20` as an example. Neither the decision log nor the founder doc says that unvalidated rates are accepted. The founder acceptance criterion in section 11, line 146 ("VAT ... are handled correctly"), points toward rejecting bad input, not against it.

Severity low is right. The trigger needs an operator typo on an optional pilot-phase CLI flag whose documented format is a fraction, the default (0.20) is correct, and the operator controls the input. Even so, the output is wrong without any warning rather than failing visibly. Only a rate of exactly -1 fails loudly, with a divide-by-zero.

confirmed.title: Bank balance staleness is measured from the period end, not from today, so a current balance is labelled 'old' when the period end is in the future
confirmed.description: A balance is marked stale when lastDay < to - 3. For a report whose period has not ended yet (for example, this month), a balance as of yesterday is compared with a date that has not arrived.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On 2026-10-09 the operator runs --from=2026-10-01 --to=2026-10-31 with a statement up to 2026-10-08. Because 2026-10-08 is before 2026-10-28, the summary says 'հին է, թարմացնել քաղվածքը' (old, refresh the statement) for a balance that is one day old.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Measure staleness against min(to, today).

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the path and the failure happens as described.

1. `ReportCommand.java:34` sets `LocalDate to = LocalDate.parse(required(args, "to"));`. Nothing compares `to` with today, clamps it, or rejects a future date.
2. `WeeklyReportService.java:75` passes that value straight through: `CashPosition cash = cashPositions.asOf(tenant, to);`.
3. `CashPositionService.java:52`: the SQL takes the latest day before `to + 1` (`occurred_at < :end`). With `to` = 2026-10-31 and a statement up to 2026-10-08, `l.day` is 2026-10-08.
4. `CashPositionService.java:75`: `boolean stale = any.day().isBefore(to.minusDays(STALE_AFTER_DAYS));`. Here 2026-10-08 is before 2026-10-28, so `stale` is true. No date from a clock or `LocalDate.now()` is used anywhere in this class.
5. `WeeklyReportService.java:160-161` then appends the label: `(a.stale() ? " · հին է, թարմացնել քաղվածքը" : "")`.

On today's date, 2026-10-09, running `--from=2026-10-01 --to=2026-10-31` with a statement ending on 2026-10-08 labels a balance that is one day old as "old, refresh the statement".

Mitigating points:
- The README (lines 107-109) documents the rule as "Older than 3 days before period end → marked stale". Measuring against the period end is therefore the intended design.
- The runbook's example uses a period that has already ended (`--to=2026-09-30`).
- The label errs on the conservative side and no money figure is distorted.

Even so, the documented rule never considers a period end in the future. In that case the output tells the operator to refresh a statement that is current, which is a misleading message. It does not cause data loss. This is a real defect of low severity, and the suggested fix (compare against `min(to, today)`) is reasonable.

Real usage can reach this. ReportCommand.run (lines 33-34) passes `--from` and `--to` straight to WeeklyReportService.generate without any check against today. WeeklyReportService line 75 then calls cashPositions.asOf(tenant, to). In CashPositionService.lastKnown (line 75), the flag is `stale = any.day().isBefore(to.minusDays(3))`, and the code never looks at the current date. WeeklyReportService line 161 adds " · հին է, թարմացնել քաղվածքը" ("old, refresh the statement") whenever a.stale() is true.

The runbook's example is a whole-month period (--from=2026-09-01 --to=2026-09-30), and the founder wants a weekly cadence. So a report on the current month or week, run on day 9 of that month (today is 2026-10-09), is a natural thing for an operator to do. With --to=2026-10-31 and a statement up to 2026-10-08, the check is 10-08 < 10-28, which is true, and a balance that is one day old is reported as old.

README line 109 does document "Older than 3 days before period end → marked stale". That rule clearly assumes the period end is already past. Applied to a period end in the future, it contradicts the founder's requirement (section 8, line 80 of the context file): call a balance old only when it actually is old, and show its true freshness. The result is a misleading freshness label telling the owner to refresh data that is already current. Other parts of the codebase do measure against today, for example KpiService line 81 and CommitService line 184, which suggests this check missed the case where the period has not ended.

The impact is limited to a misleading label: the balance number itself is still correct. Low severity stands.

The code does what the finding says. CashPositionService.java:75 computes `stale = lastDay < to - 3`, and WeeklyReportService appends "հին է, թարմացնել քաղվածքը" when that flag is set. rejected.title: An MT940 :86: continuation line starting with ':NN:' is taken as a new field (can reassign the account or split the statement)
why:
The code does what the finding says. In Mt940Parser.java, tokenize() checks every non-blank line against FIELD = "^:(\d{2}[A-Z]?):(.*)$" (line 27). A match runs `out.add(new String[]{m.group(1), m.group(2)})` (line 126). Only a line that does not match gets appended to the previous field (lines 127-129). So a :86: continuation line written as ":20:invoice 77" becomes a new ["20", ...] field, and in parse() `case "20" -> st = new Statement(value.trim())` (line 52) throws away the current statement. The next :61: then fails at line 63 (":61: before opening balance"), or :62F: fails at line 97 because running == null. Either way the file is rejected. A ":25:..." continuation line would hit `case "25" -> requireStatement(st, tag).account = value.trim()` (line 53), and later :61: rows in that statement would read the new s.account at line 77.

I still refute it as a defect, for two reasons:
(1) The input breaks the SWIFT FIN format. In SWIFT FIN, a line that starts with ':' marks the start of a new field, and continuation lines of a field (including :86: free text) must not begin with ':' or '-'. So "line starting with :NN: = new field" is the standard tokenization rule. A SWIFT-compliant MT940 cannot contain this input. README line 91 says: "The tag structure is the SWIFT standard". No compliant exporter will produce the stated input.
(2) The main scenario the finding verified (":20:" inside :86:) fails safe. The whole file is rejected and nothing is written, as decision #13 requires. There is no data loss or wrong figure; the only problem is that the error message is less helpful.

The silent case, a ":25:" continuation line, needs a bank to export a malformed file that by chance has a valid-looking account tag at the start of a free-text line. Nothing in the code or docs shows that happening. Even then it only changes the masked account label (account_ref, plus the account part of idColumns). Amounts and balances are not affected, and the balance check still has to pass.

This is a hypothetical robustness concern about non-SWIFT input, not a concrete defect with a realistic failure scenario.

The code does work as described. tokenize() (Mt940Parser.java:119-133) starts a new field on any line matching ^:(\d{2}[A-Z]?):, including lines inside :86: free text. But the failing input is one a real bank file should not contain. SWIFT FIN's general field-format rules forbid ':' (and '-') as the first character of any line of field content, because a line starting with ':' is how a new tag begins. Banks produce MT940 (including the Ameriabank export cited in the vault) with SWIFT-compliant formatters, which follow this rule when wrapping :86: at 65 characters. So a continuation line that begins with ':NN:' is non-standard input. Any tag-based MT940 parser, Prowide included, would read it the same way.

When the bad input does appear, the result is mostly harmless:
- A ':20:' line opens a new Statement. The old statement never reaches its :62F:, so its rows are never committed. The new statement then hits ':61: before opening balance' or a closing-balance mismatch and the whole file is rejected with nothing written. This fails closed and loses no data.
- A ':61:' or ':6xx:' line must match the strict LINE/BALANCE regexes or the file is rejected.
- Unhandled tags fall into the ignored default branch. The only effect is a shorter description.

The one silent case is a ':25:' continuation line. That needs bank free text that happens to start a wrapped line with exactly ':25:', which breaks the colon rule above. Nothing in the tests, fixtures or README suggests any target bank emits that. A defect that needs input violating the format's own syntax, and that otherwise fails closed, is not realistically reachable.

1) What the code does. `ReportCommand` builds `KpiSettings` from the command-line flags. So the run is technically possible.

2) It needs a false assertion from the operator. `--formulas-confirmed=true` means "accountant signed off" (comment in `KpiSettings.java`). `--formulas-confirmed=true` is how the founder's "confirm the 2,000 with the accountant" step is recorded. Conclusion: the failure needs the operator to falsely claim accountant sign-off, and the output still labels the zero variable cost as an assumption. This is documented, intended behaviour, not a reachable defect.

rejected.title: The test named roundedHalfUp cannot detect HALF_EVEN or premature 2-decimal rounding
why:
I checked the arithmetic and it is correct. In KpiServiceIT, the test netSales_grossProfit_withReturnDiscountAndVat_roundedHalfUp uses one sale group, (70000-5000)/1.2 = 54166.666..., and one return group, 35000/1.2 = 29166.666.... Neither value is a .xx5 tie, so HALF_UP, HALF_EVEN, HALF_DOWN and CEILING all give the same results. Rounding each group to 2 decimals first gives 54166.67 - 29166.67 = 25000.00, the same as full precision.
